entries.text: The temporary power or prominence a planet gains from its chart position—such as being placed near an angle, moving at fast speed, or forming favorable aspects—rather than its sign placement.

A stressful or challenging geometric relationship (such as a square, opposition, or harsh conjunction) formed between planets, particularly involving traditional malefic bodies, indicating friction or obstacles.

The four crucial structural pivot points in a chart—the Ascendant (1st house cusp), Imum Coeli / IC (4th house cusp), Descendant (7th house cusp), and Midheaven / MC (10th house cusp)—which mark the directions of the horizon and meridian, conferring high visibility and power to planets placed near them.
A classical predictive technique that advances the rising sign by one zodiac sign per year of life, identifying the specific planet that acts as the primary "Lord of the Year".
An aspect where a faster-moving planet is actively traveling toward an exact degree alignment with another planet or point, signifying building energy and impending events.

The exact degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment and location of birth; it forms the cusp of the First House and symbolizes physical appearance, personal identity, and outward demeanor.
The geometric distance measured in degrees between two or more planets or chart points, showing how their psychological energies interact.
Minor planetary bodies (such as Ceres, Pallas, Juno, and Vesta) orbiting between Mars and Jupiter, used in astrology to refine specific thematic archetypes.

A state in traditional astrology where two planets occupy signs that share no recognized geometric aspect (such as semi-sextiles or inconjuncts), leaving them unable to "see" or relate to one another.
Planets traditionally recognized as supportive, fortunate, and harmonious—specifically Venus (the Lesser Benefic) and Jupiter (the Greater Benefic).
A stressful condition where a planet is trapped between two malefic planets (Mars and Saturn) either by body or aspect, restricting its freedom of movement and expression.
The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which fall away from the angular houses; planets here are considered quieter, inward-focused, or less direct in physical expression.
Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn—the four signs that initiate the seasons, representing drive, leadership, initiative, and outgoing action.
An exceptionally fortunate condition where a planet is positioned within 17 minutes of arc of the exact center of the Sun, absorbing immense vitality rather than being burned by solar heat.
A planet positioned within approximately 3 degrees (or up to 8–10 degrees) of the Sun, where its independent expression is obscured or weakened by solar glare.
A major aspect formed when two or more planets occupy the same degree or sign (0° apart), blending and concentrating their forces into a single impulse.
The exact boundary line separating one zodiac sign or house from the next; planets positioned on a cusp carry heightened potency for that area of life.
A 10-degree subdivision of a 30-degree zodiac sign (yielding 36 decans across the zodiac), each ruled by a specific planetary face that fine-tunes its expression.
The angular distance of a planet north or south of the celestial equator, measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds.
The comprehensive art and procedure of synthesizing and interpreting chart factors into a cohesive reading.
The point on the western horizon directly opposite the Ascendant, marking the cusp of the Seventh House and representing marriage, close partnerships, and open interactions.
An essential debility occurring when a planet resides in the sign opposite its home sign (domicile), forcing it to operate in an environment foreign to its natural temperament.
The normal, forward progression of a planet moving through the degrees of the zodiac.
A planet that rules the sign occupied by another planet or house cusp, holding managerial authority over that visiting planet's expression.
A chart cast for a daytime birth (Sun above the horizon); planets belonging to the diurnal sect (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn) operate with greater comfort in day charts.
The apparent yearly path of the Sun across the sky around which the twelve zodiac signs are aligned.
The four fundamental cosmic building blocks—Fire, Earth, Air, and Water—that categorize the twelve signs into shared temperaments.
A calculated table or reference book recording the daily positions, longitudes, and declinations of celestial bodies over time.
The intrinsic strength or dignity a planet possesses based on its exact degree placement within its home sign (domicile), exaltation, triplicity, term, or face.
An essential dignity where a planet is elevated like an honored guest in a sign whose environment amplifies its virtues.
An essential debility occurring in the sign directly opposite a planet's exaltation, where its energy feels restricted or out of place.
A classical Persian and Arabic time-lord system that divides a person's lifespan into fixed, sequential chapters ruled by specific planets based on whether birth occurred during the day or night.
Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius—the middle signs of each season that stabilize energy, signifying persistence, determination, and focus.
A traditional shorthand symbol used to depict a planet, sign, or aspect on a chart wheel.
A dynamic aspect pattern formed by four planets making four squares and two oppositions across the chart, generating intense motivation and life challenge.
A harmonious aspect pattern formed by three planets positioned 120 degrees apart in signs of the same element, creating an effortless, flowing circuit of talent.
One of twelve sectors dividing a birth chart, each governing specific categories of human life experience, such as personal identity, finances, family, or career.
A mathematical framework (such as Placidus, Whole Sign, Koch, or Regiomontanus) used to divide the 360-degree chart wheel into twelve distinct houses.
The lowest point of the meridian at the bottom of the chart, marking the cusp of the Fourth House and representing roots, heritage, private life, and home.
An aspect connecting planets 150 degrees apart (five signs away), creating subtle tension that demands ongoing adjustment between incompatible energies.
The precise moment a celestial body crosses the threshold into a new zodiac sign or house.
A zodiac sign completely enclosed within a wide house without appearing on either house cusp.
The Sun and the Moon—the two primary sources of light in the sky that anchor core identity and emotional life in a horoscope.
Planets traditionally associated with challenge, boundaries, or friction—specifically Mars (the Lesser Malefic) and Saturn (the Greater Malefic).
The highest point of the chart meridian above the horizon, marking the cusp of the Tenth House and representing public standing, ambition, and career.
The structural classification of signs into Cardinal, Fixed, or Mutable modes, dictating how planetary energy is initiated, sustained, or adapted.
Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces—signs that conclude the seasons, representing flexibility, adaptability, and transition.
A supportive relationship formed when two planets occupy each other's home signs or exaltations, allowing them to assist one another.
A two-dimensional map of the heavens calculated for the exact moment, date, and geographic location of birth.
The mathematical intersection points where the Moon's orbital path crosses the ecliptic; associated with life trajectory, growth, and karmic lessons.
A major 180-degree aspect between planets in opposite signs, bringing tension, awareness, or relationship confrontation.
The allowable margin of error or degree range around an exact aspect angle within which two planets still exert an influence on each other.
A planet that possesses no essential dignities or debilities in its current sign, functioning like a visitor without established roots or duties.
A traditional predictive system that calculates events by rotating natal points along the celestial equator based on Earth's diurnal rotation at the key of one degree per year of life.
A predictive method where each day of planetary movement following birth equates to one year of life, charting internal emotional and psychological evolution.
The four major sections of a birth chart divided by the horizon and meridian axes (Houses 1–3, 4–6, 7–9, and 10–12).
A condition where a host planet receiving another body into its sign or dignity provides support, virtue, and backing to that visiting planet.
The apparent backward movement of a planet across the sky caused by Earth's relative orbital speed, encouraging reflection and review.
The state where a planet resides in the sign it naturally rules, granting it full authority, ease, and comfort of expression.
An aspect where two planets move away from each other after reaching exact degree alignment, reflecting past conditions or receding events.
A supportive major aspect of 60 degrees (two signs apart) that creates opportunities, communication, and pleasant flow.
A horoscope calculated for the exact annual moment when the transiting Sun returns to the precise degree, minute, and second of its natal placement.
A challenging major aspect of 90 degrees (three signs apart) that generates internal friction, dynamic tension, and a drive to take physical action.
The moment a planet appears to pause in the sky as it changes direction between direct and retrograde motion.
A cluster of three or more planets conjoined in a single sign or house, concentrating intense focus in that life sector.
The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which follow the angular houses; associated with resource consolidation, stability, and security.
The practice of overlaying and comparing two individual birth charts to evaluate relationship compatibility and mutual dynamics.
Unequal 5-fold subdivisions of each zodiac sign ruled by the five traditional planets (excluding the luminaries), granting specific behavioral boundaries to planets residing within them.
A planet activated by a specific predictive technique (such as Annual Profections or Firdaria) to govern as the primary ruler of events for a given period of life.
The real-time, ongoing movements of planets in the sky as they form geometric aspects to the static positions in a natal chart.
A highly favorable major aspect of 120 degrees (four signs apart in the same element) that brings natural talent, harmony, and unearned ease.
The state of a planet (most notably the Moon) when it will form no further major applying aspects before leaving its current sign, indicating a period where actions may not yield expected results.
A special aspect pattern formed by two planets in a 60-degree sextile, both casting 150-degree quincunx aspects to a third focal planet, signaling a fated turning point or special life mission.
An imaginary, infinite sphere surrounding the Earth upon which all stars, constellations, and planetary positions are projected for astronomical measurement and chart calculation.
The apparent yearly orbital path of the Sun across the sky as viewed from Earth, forming the central 360° geometric plane around which the zodiac is measured.

A narrow celestial belt extending approximately 8° north and 8° south of the ecliptic (16° wide in total), which encompasses the maximum orbital inclinations and paths of all visible planets and the Moon.
The direct projection of Earth's terrestrial equator outward into space; its two points of intersection with the ecliptic establish the equinoxes.
The constant tilt of Earth’s rotational axis relative to the plane of its orbit around the Sun (approximately 23°27'), which gives rise to terrestrial seasons and uneven sign ascension times.

The great circle passing through the center of the Earth perpendicular to an observer's local Zenith and Nadir, dividing the celestial sphere into upper (visible/diurnal) and lower (hidden/nocturnal) hemispheres.

The vertical north-south great circle passing through the terrestrial poles, celestial poles, and the observer’s local Zenith and Nadir; it divides the chart into eastern (oriental) and western (occidental) hemispheres.

The exact astronomical point on the celestial sphere located directly 90° overhead an observer; distinct from the astrological Midheaven (MC), which measures where the meridian intersects the ecliptic.
The astronomical point on the celestial sphere directly beneath the observer’s feet (180° opposite the Zenith).
The celestial meridian line passing through the celestial poles and both equinox points.
The celestial meridian line passing through the celestial poles and both solstice points.

entries.section: 3. The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The four fundamental structural pillars of a horoscope—Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli—derived from the intersections of the local horizon and meridian with the ecliptic.

entries.section: 3. The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The exact degree of the zodiac intersecting the eastern horizon at the moment and geographic location of birth; forms the First House cusp and symbolizes physical embodiment and personality.

entries.section: 3. The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The degree of the zodiac setting on the western horizon directly 180° opposite the Ascendant; forms the Seventh House cusp and symbolizes interpersonal relating and partnerships.

entries.section: 3. The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The highest point of culmination where the observer's local meridian intersects the ecliptic above the Earth; forms the Tenth House cusp in quadrant house systems and represents public life and career.

entries.section: 3. The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The lowest point of anti-culmination where the meridian intersects the ecliptic beneath the Earth; forms the Fourth House cusp and represents home, family, and inner roots.
Distance measured eastward along the ecliptic from 0° Aries through 360° across the twelve 30° zodiac signs.
The angular distance of a planet or star measured in degrees north (+) or south (-) from the plane of the ecliptic.
Spatial distance measured along the celestial equator in hours, minutes, and seconds (or 0°–360°) eastward starting from the Vernal Equinox (0° Aries).
The vertical distance of a celestial body measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds north (+) or south (-) of the celestial equator.
The degree of the celestial equator that ascends above the eastern horizon simultaneously with a given degree of the ecliptic at a specific terrestrial latitude.
The apparent 24-hour rotation of the entire celestial sphere from east to west around the Earth’s axis, causing stars and signs to rise, culminate, and set daily.
The natural counter-clockwise forward movement of planets along the zodiac band from west to east along their respective orbits.

The slow, backward wobbling shift of Earth's rotational axis relative to the fixed stars (~50.26" of arc per year), causing the Vernal Equinox to recede through the zodiac constellations over a ~25,800-year cycle.
The complete ~25,800-year precessional cycle required for the Vernal Equinox to travel backward through all twelve zodiacal constellations (each "Great Month" or Age lasting ~2,150 years).
The exact passage of a planet or star across the observer's local meridian, reaching its highest altitude above the horizon.
The seasonal zodiac framework anchored strictly to the Vernal Equinox (0° Aries = Spring Equinox), aligning sign boundaries with Earth’s solar cycle.
The constellation-based zodiac framework anchored directly to physical fixed star patterns, accounting for precessional drift.
Zodiac signs that take significantly longer than 2 hours to rise over the eastern horizon in Northern latitudes (Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius) due to the obliquity of the ecliptic.
Zodiac signs that rise rapidly in under 2 hours in Northern latitudes (Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, Gemini).
An astronomical or astrological viewpoint taken from the center of the Earth, mapping celestial movements as experienced humanly from terrestrial ground.
An astronomical viewpoint centered on the Sun, mapping physical planetary orbits through space.
The four primary 180° divisions of a chart created by the Horizon (Superior/Visible vs. Inferior/Hidden) and the Meridian (Oriental/Eastern vs. Occidental/Western).
The four 90° sectors of a chart wheel bounded by the horizontal and vertical axes (1st Quadrant: Houses 1–3; 2nd Quadrant: Houses 4–6; 3rd Quadrant: Houses 7–9; 4th Quadrant: Houses 10–12).
An calculated almanac or data matrix recording daily planetary longitudes, declinations, and orbital speeds for chart calculation.
The primary twofold division of the zodiac into alternating active and receptive signs, reflecting the fundamental Hermetic law of polarity.
Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius. Associated with the Fire and Air elements, these signs are characteristically active, centrifugal, outward-projecting, assertive, and expressive.
Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces. Associated with the Earth and Water elements, these signs are centripetal, receptive, self-contained, magnetic, and reflective.
A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element, positioned 120° apart across the zodiac to form an equilateral triangle.
Aries, Leo, Sagittarius. Defined temperamentally as hot and dry. Governs vitality, enthusiasm, spirit, willpower, and dynamic self-expression.
Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn. Defined temperamentally as cold and dry. Governs physical form, material security, stability, concrete efficiency, and tangible results.
Gemini, Libra, Aquarius. Defined temperamentally as hot and moist. Governs intellect, communication, social interaction, conceptual thought, and objectivity.
Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces. Defined temperamentally as cold and moist. Governs feeling, intuition, subconscious drives, emotional empathy, and healing.
A structural classification of four signs sharing a common mode of action and seasonal function.
Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn. Aligned with the beginning of the four seasons. Represents initiation, trailblazing, leadership, ambition, and driving energy forward.
Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius. Aligned with the middle peak of each season. Represents stability, concentration of power, stamina, perseverance, and resistance to external change.
Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. Aligned with the transition at the end of each season. Represents flexibility, adaptability, versatility, transition, and resourcefulness.
Gemini, Sagittarius, Pisces (and Virgo in classical tradition). Signs represented by dual figures, denoting versatility, dual nature, or simultaneous pursuits.
Aries and Libra, whose beginning marks the spring and autumnal equinoxes when day and night are equal.
Cancer and Capricorn, marking the summer and winter solstices where the Sun reaches its maximum northern and southern declination.
Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius (second half), and Capricorn—signs represented by four-legged animals.
Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Aquarius, and Sagittarius (first half)—signs depicted as human figures, associated with social intelligence, communication, and reasoning.
Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces—the water signs, traditionally associated with emotional introspection, deep feeling, and non-verbal expression.
Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces—water signs associated with emotional abundance, growth, and reproduction.
Gemini, Leo, and Virgo—signs traditionally associated with dryness, austerity, or lack of physical yield.
Cardinal Fire (Masculine/Yang) — The pioneering, dynamic, independent spark of action.
Fixed Earth (Feminine/Yin) — The steady, sensual, grounded, and persistent builder.
Mutable Air (Masculine/Yang) — The curious, versatile, swift, and communicative mind.
Cardinal Water (Feminine/Yin) — The protective, nurturing, intuitive, and feeling initiator.
Fixed Fire (Masculine/Yang) — The radiant, creative, loyal, and dignified center of power.
Mutable Earth (Feminine/Yin) — The analytical, precise, practical, and service-minded reflector.
Cardinal Air (Masculine/Yang) — The diplomatic, harmonious, social, and aesthetic bridge-builder.
Fixed Water (Feminine/Yin) — The intense, magnetic, transformative, and emotionally deep investigator.
Mutable Fire (Masculine/Yang) — The adventurous, philosophical, expansive, and truth-seeking idealist.
Cardinal Earth (Feminine/Yin) — The ambitious, disciplined, structured, and pragmatic authority.
Fixed Air (Masculine/Yang) — The objective, visionary, humanitarian, and individualistic thinker.
Mutable Water (Feminine/Yin) — The compassionate, imaginative, transcendent, and empathic mystic.

entries.term: Luminaries (The Lights / Lights of the Horoscope)
entries.text: The Sun and the Moon. They are not astronomically planets, but in astrology, they form the primary core of consciousness, vitality, physical embodiment, and emotional life.
The kingly light of the diurnal chart. Governs the core ego, conscious purpose, creative vitality, spirit (daimon), willpower, identity, and the father archetype.
The queenly light of the nocturnal chart. Governs the instinctual mind, subconscious habit patterns, physical body, emotional memory, mothering, instinctual safety, and the lunation cycle.
The Messenger. Governs cognitive processing, perception, language, speech, intellect, commerce, short-distance travel, adaptability, and mental synthesis.
The Lesser Benefic. Governs personal values, attraction, aesthetic beauty, social harmony, romantic connection, intimacy, pleasure, and artistic expression.
The Lesser Malefic. Governs physical drive, assertion, ambition, sexual energy, competitive spirit, courage, conflict, boundaries, and executive action.
The Greater Benefic. Governs expansion, wisdom, philosophy, higher education, abundance, faith, ethics, luck, and spiritual seeking.
The Greater Malefic. Governs structure, discipline, boundaries, time (Chronos), responsibility, maturity, long-term mastery, karma, and contraction.
The Awakener. Governs sudden breakthroughs, innovation, rebellion, individual liberty, eccentricity, technological advancement, and radical shift.
The Mystic. Governs divine inspiration, spiritual transcendence, imagination, dreams, glamor, illusion, compassion, and the dissolution of ego boundaries.
The Regenerator. Governs psychological depth, power dynamics, death and rebirth, transformation, shadow integration, catharsis, and unearthing hidden truths.
A Centaur body orbiting between Saturn and Uranus. Represents the core soul wound, spiritual mentorship, healing through vulnerability, and bridging physical structure with spiritual awakening.
The Great Mother asteroid. Governs physical nurturing, grief, loss, harvest, maternal bonding, unconditional love, and self-care.
The Warrior Queen asteroid. Governs strategic intellect, pattern recognition, visual arts, creative problem-solving, diplomacy, and justice.
The Sacred Partner asteroid. Governs committed partnership, marriage dynamics, soulmate contracts, relational equity, boundaries, and jealousy.
The Keeper of the Sacred Flame asteroid. Governs sacred focus, devotion, dedication, spiritual purity, sexual alchemy, and independence.
The Goddess of Discord. A trans-Neptunian dwarf planet representing raw truth-telling, disruptive boundary-breaking, standing up for the marginalized, and holy rage.
The northern intersection of the Moon's orbit and the ecliptic. Represents soul growth, future trajectory, spiritual appetite, unfamiliar territory, and evolutionary direction.
The southern intersection of the Moon's orbit and the ecliptic. Represents past momentum, innate gifts, unconscious comfort zones, karmic baggage, and points of spiritual release.
The calculated lunar apogee (the point where the Moon is farthest from Earth). Represents raw instinct, unbridled power, refusal to submit to oppression, repressed shadow, and sacred independence.
A calculated Arabic Lot combining the longitudes of the Ascendant, Sun, and Moon. Represents physical well-being, material flow, prosperity, and the harmonious integration of mind, body, and spirit.
The normal, forward progression of a planet moving counter-clockwise through the degrees of the zodiac.
The apparent backward motion of a planet caused by Earth's relative orbital speed, internalizing the planet's archetype and calling for review, reflection, and recalculation.
The exact moment a planet appears to freeze in longitude before shifting direction; planets at station exert maximum concentration of energy.
A planet located within ~8.5° of the Sun, where its visibility and independent expression are obscured by intense solar glare.

entries.term: Cazimi (In the Heart of the Sun)
entries.text: A planet positioned within 17 minutes of arc of the exact center of the Sun, granting it supreme solar audience, empowerment, and clarity.
A planet positioned within ~15° of the Sun, entering a state of partial weakening or concealment before or after combustion.
A planet that rises before the Sun in the dawn sky, operating with initiative, outward projection, and forward momentum.
A planet that sets after the Sun in the twilight sky, operating with reflection, evaluation, and receptive processing.
A planet moving faster or slower than its average daily orbital speed, heightening or delaying its worldly impact.
The first morning a planet or fixed star becomes visible on the eastern horizon at dawn after having been obscured by the Sun's glare.
The last evening a planet or star is visible on the western horizon at dusk before disappearing into the Sun's light.
Venus (Lesser Benefic) and Jupiter (Greater Benefic)—bodies that naturally unify, expand, harmonize, and support human experience.
Mars (Lesser Malefic) and Saturn (Greater Malefic)—bodies that naturally challenge, sever, limit, discipline, and test human resilience.

The ancient division of planets into two cosmic teams. The Day Sect (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn) operates best in day charts; the Night Sect (Moon, Venus, Mars) operates best in night charts. Mercury is adaptable based on its orientation to the Sun.
Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto—planets whose orbits lie outside Earth's orbit around the Sun.
Mercury and Venus—planets whose orbits lie inside Earth's orbit around the Sun.
The planet that rules the zodiac sign on the Ascendant, acting as the primary pilot and director of the native's life path.

Discovered in 1977 by Charles Kowal, Chiron orbits between Saturn and Uranus. Officially categorized with dual status as a comet (95P) and minor planet (2060), Chiron serves as a symbolic bridge between personal Saturnian boundaries and transpersonal Uranus awakening, signifying systemic soul wounds, mentorship, and compassionate understanding.

The first and largest asteroid discovered (1801), recently classified as a dwarf planet. Governs agricultural harvest, physical and emotional nurturing, grief, hospice care, food/eating dynamics, and the deep, bittersweet Mother-Child separation bond.
Goddess of wisdom, justice, and diplomacy. Represents cool, logical strategy, father/daughter mentorship bonds, pattern recognition, and business/political acumen without emotional interference.
Goddess of marriage and fidelity. Symbolizes total relational commitment, partnership equity, and the complex emotional dynamics of loyalty, jealousy, and boundaries.

entries.term: Vesta (The Keeper of the Sacred Flame)
entries.text: Goddess of the hearth and sanctuary. Represents absolute devotion, sacred focus, spiritual purity, sexual alchemy, and the need for periodic retreat to recharge personal energy.
A Centaur body discovered in 1992. Presides over "tipping points," radical transformations, unlocking hidden potential, and releasing inherited or ancestral processes.
A Centaur body associated with power dynamics, tie-cutting, ending toxic patterns, and resolving deep-seated, ancestral oppression or karmic ties.
A Centaur body entering Uranus's sphere; mythologically the wife of Chiron, holding a remarkably stable orbit that symbolizes compassionate space-holding.
An asteroid associated with erotic attraction, passion, and personal magnetism.

entries.term: Trans-Neptunian & Kuiper Belt Objects (Eris, Quaoar, Sedna, Ixion, Varuna, Orcus)
entries.text: Newly discovered outer-system dwarf planets and bodies that reflect deep generational shifts, collective rites of passage, and primordial evolutionary forces.

Measures the distance from the Sun to the Moon by day (or Moon to Sun by night) projected from the Ascendant. Governs physical embodiment, health, material possessions, environment, and worldly livelihood.
Calculated inversely to Fortune (Moon to Sun by day; Sun to Moon by night). Governs the soul, intellect (phronesis), intentional action, career direction, and moral purpose.

Measures the distance from the Lot of Spirit to Venus by day (reversed by night) projected from the Ascendant. Governs personal desires, appetites, friendship, mutual attraction, and favor. (Note: Classical variants by Valens and Dorotheus calculate Eros using the arc between Fortune and Spirit).

Measures the distance from Mercury to the Lot of Fortune by day (reversed by night) projected from the Ascendant. Governs constraints, struggles, subordinations, inevitable fate, and competitive enmities.
Measures the distance from Mars to the Lot of Fortune by day (reversed by night) projected from the Ascendant. Governs boldness, physical strength, risk-taking, and martial action.
Measures the distance from the Lot of Spirit to Jupiter by day (reversed by night) projected from the Ascendant. Governs faith, good hope, generosity, enterprise, and prosperous outcomes.

Measures the distance from Saturn to the Lot of Fortune by day (reversed by night) projected from the Ascendant. Governs hidden matters, retribution, structural weakness, exile, loss, and karmic boundaries.
A calculated synthesis of Fortune and Spirit that reveals an individual's baseline underlying stability and potential for public eminence.
Calculated from the Ascendant using Sun/Saturn (for the Father) and Moon/Venus (for the Mother) to evaluate parental legacy and ancestral lineage.
Projected using the angular distances between Jupiter/Venus and the Moon to assess progeny and creative inheritance.
Calculated using the 7th House cusp or Venus/Sun/Moon angles to assess contractual partnerships and marital harmony.
Projected using Mercury and the Sun/Ascendant to assess trade, financial transactions, and business success.
Sensitive points calculated to pinpoint bodily vulnerabilities, physical crises, or legal accusations.

entries.term: Lot of Death & End of Matters
entries.text: Calculated using the 8th House cusp and the Moon to evaluate life transitions and final conditions.
The calculated lunar apogee (the point of the Moon's orbit farthest from Earth). Symbolizes raw instinct, refusal to submit to societal suppression, untamed power, and shadow integration.
A calculated point representing spiritual illumination, grace, protection, and uncorrupted virtue.
The western intersection of the Prime Vertical and the Ecliptic. Acts as a "second Descendant," representing turning points, fated encounters, and relationship catalysts.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The four critical power points of a horoscope—the Ascendant (ASC), Midheaven (MC), Descendant (DSC), and Imum Coeli (IC). Planets positioned on or near the angles gain immense strength, visibility, and accidental dignity.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The exact degree of the zodiac intersecting the eastern horizon at the moment and latitude of birth; marks the cusp of the First House. Functions as the "Front Door" of the chart, representing physical appearance, personal identity, vitality, personal outlook, and first impressions.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The highest point of culmination where the meridian intersects the ecliptic above the Earth; marks the cusp of the Tenth House in quadrant systems. Functions as the "Roof" of the chart, governing career, social standing, public reputation, vocation, and public ambition.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The exact degree of the zodiac setting on the western horizon directly 180° opposite the Ascendant; marks the cusp of the Seventh House. Functions as the "Back Door" of the chart, symbolizing one-on-one partnerships, marriage, legal contracts, and social interactions.

entries.term: Imum Coeli (IC / Hypogeon / Bottom of the Sky)
entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The lowest point of anti-culmination where the meridian intersects the ecliptic beneath the Earth; marks the cusp of the Fourth House. Functions as the "Cellar" or private foundation, governing roots, home, family, ancestry, early conditioning, and the end of life.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The point on the ecliptic located exactly 90° behind the Ascendant, marking the true highest mathematical point of the ecliptic arc above the horizon. In the Equal House system, the nonagesimal serves as the cusp of the 10th house.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The astronomical intersection of the observer's local north-south meridian line with the ecliptic. In quadrant house systems, this exact degree defines the 10th house cusp.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: The degree of the ecliptic that would be rising if the birth occurred at the Earth's equator; used as the 1st house cusp in the Meridian house system.

entries.section: The Four Primary Angles (Cardines / Power Points)
entries.text: An auxiliary polar axis formed by the intersection of the Prime Vertical with the Ecliptic on the western (Vertex) and eastern (Antivertex) horizons. Symbolizes fated encounters, sudden relationship turnarounds, and systemic catalysts.

entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: An angular house governing physical embodiment, personality traits, health, personal vitality, self-image, and new beginnings.

entries.term: Second House (Anaphora / Gate of Hades / House of Possessions)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A succedent house governing personal finances, liquid assets, earned income, personal values, material security, and self-worth.

entries.term: Third House (Goddess / House of Siblings & Mind)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A cadent house governing short-distance travel, siblings, mental equipment, daily communication, local environment, and early schooling.

entries.term: Fourth House (Hypogeon / House of Home & Ancestry)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: An angular house governing roots, parents, family background, domestic life, physical real estate, private emotions, and final conditions of life.

entries.term: Fifth House (Good Fortune / House of Pleasure & Procreation)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A succedent house governing children, creative expression, romance, speculation, entertainment, hobbies, and personal joy.

entries.term: Sixth House (Bad Fortune / House of Service & Health)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A cadent house governing daily routine work, employment, physical illness, hygiene, service, pets, and necessary adjustments.

entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: An angular house governing marriage, committed partnerships, business associates, legal contracts, open enemies, and public relations.

entries.term: Eighth House (Idle Place / House of Transformation & Shared Assets)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A succedent house governing joint resources, partner's finances, inheritances, taxes, birth, death, psychological rebirth, and occult forces.

entries.term: Ninth House (God / House of Philosophy & Higher Travel)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A cadent house governing long-distance travel, higher education, philosophy, religion, ethics, publishing, and spiritual seeking.

entries.term: Tenth House (Medium Coeli / House of Career & Standing)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: An angular house governing public career, social status, reputation, professional achievements, authority figures, and life calling.

entries.term: Eleventh House (Good Spirit / House of Friends & Hopes)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A succedent house governing social networks, friendships, alliances, community causes, hopes, wishes, and career gains.

entries.term: Twelfth House (Bad Spirit / House of Solitude & Undoing)
entries.section: The Twelve Houses (Dodekatropos / Spheres of Experience)
entries.text: A cadent house governing solitude, mental health, institutions, hidden self-sabotage, spiritual surrender, loss, and hidden enemies.

Houses whose cusps coincide with the four major angles. Associated with cardinal energy, immediate physical action, high visibility, self-activation, and primary life structures. Planets placed here possess maximum accidental dignity and dynamic power.

Houses that follow or "succeed" the angular houses as the sky rotates. Associated with fixed energy, consolidation of resources, stability, personal desire, and financial/emotional security. Planets here have moderate, steady strength.

Houses that "fall away" (cadere) from the angular positions due to diurnal rotation. Associated with mutable energy, mental adaptation, learning, observation, exchange of ideas, and background preparation. Planets here have the lowest direct physical power, operating inwardly or mentally.
Below the horizon line; indicates subjective, personal, introspective, and private developmental focus.
Above the horizon line; indicates objective, public, social, and outer-directed focus.
Surrounding the Ascendant; indicates self-determination, personal initiative, and taking destiny into one's own hands.
Surrounding the Descendant; indicates relationship orientation, social adaptation, and life heavily influenced by others.

• 1st Quadrant (Houses 1–3): Personal development, physical self, personal data, and emergence.
• 2nd Quadrant (Houses 4–6): Unconscious growth, home foundation, personal creativity, and self-mastery.
• 3rd Quadrant (Houses 7–9): Self-expansion, awareness of others, partnerships, and social identity.
• 4th Quadrant (Houses 10–12): Public integration, social expression, collective contribution, and self-transcendence.
Corresponds to Fire signs; governs personal vitality, creative joy, self-expression, and spiritual expansion.
Corresponds to Earth signs; governs finances, daily work, material stability, professional security, and tangible results.
Corresponds to Air signs; governs intellectual exchange, social associations, partnerships, networking, and community integration.
Corresponds to Water signs; governs emotional roots, subconscious urges, deep transformation, inner healing, and spiritual growth.
The 1st house governs the mind, persona, and head; Mercury, as the messenger of intellect and speech, thrives at the rising point.

entries.term: Moon Rejoices in the 3rd House (House of the Goddess)
entries.text: The Moon rules change, movement, short journeys, and daily habits; it rejoices in the 3rd house of local environment and communication.

entries.term: Venus Rejoices in the 5th House (House of Good Fortune)
entries.text: Venus rules pleasure, love, aesthetics, and romance; it rejoices in the 5th house of creativity and procreation.

entries.term: Mars Rejoices in the 6th House (House of Bad Fortune)
entries.text: Mars, the malefic planet of war and severing, rejoices in the 6th house of illness, servitude, and struggle, where its harsh energy can be put to work.

entries.term: Sun Rejoices in the 9th House (House of God)
entries.text: The Sun, source of light and spiritual truth, rejoices in the 9th house of higher wisdom, philosophy, and divine foresight.

entries.term: Jupiter Rejoices in the 11th House (House of Good Spirit)
entries.text: Jupiter, the Greater Benefic of abundance, rejoices in the 11th house of hopes, allies, patronage, and supportive networks.

entries.term: Saturn Rejoices in the 12th House (House of Bad Spirit)
entries.text: Saturn, the Greater Malefic of boundaries and isolation, rejoices in the 12th house of solitude, confinement, and tribulations.

The joys reflect perfect sect balance—all diurnal planets (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn) have their joys above the horizon (9th, 11th, 12th), while all nocturnal planets (Moon, Venus, Mars) have their joys below the horizon (3rd, 5th, 6th).

Classical doctrine where placing a planet in the house directly opposite its place of joy (e.g., Jupiter in the 5th, Venus in the 11th, Sun in the 3rd) places it in its "sorrow," creating a structural handicap.

entries.term: Whole Sign House System (Sign-House System / Dodekatropos)
entries.text: The oldest known system of house division, dating back to 1st-century BCE Hellenistic astrology. The entire zodiac sign containing the calculated Ascendant degree becomes the 1st House from 0° to 30°, and each subsequent sign becomes the next house in sequence. The Midheaven degree floats independently as a sensitive point and does not define the 10th house cusp.

Takes the exact degree of the Ascendant as the 1st house cusp, and projects that identical degree across all subsequent consecutive signs (e.g., if ASC is 14° Taurus, 2nd cusp is 14° Gemini, 3rd cusp is 14° Cancer). Every house is exactly 30° long. The MC floats as a sensitive point rather than anchoring the 10th cusp.

One of the oldest quadrant systems, attributed to the 3rd-century philosopher Porphyry. Directly measures the ecliptic longitude arc between the Ascendant and Midheaven in each quadrant and trisects that arc into three equal longitudinal segments to find the intermediate cusps (2nd, 3rd, 5th, 6th, 8th, 9th, 11th, 12th).

entries.section: 3. Quadrant Systems: Spatial / Great Circle Division
entries.text: Attributed to 13th-century mathematician Johannes Campanus (though known earlier as the "System of Hermes"). Divides the observer's Prime Vertical (the vertical great circle passing through the Zenith and Nadir) into twelve equal 30° arcs using great circles passing through the North and South points of the horizon. Where these "slices" cut the ecliptic forms the house cusps.

entries.section: 3. Quadrant Systems: Spatial / Great Circle Division
entries.text: Formulated by 15th-century mathematician Johann Müller (Regiomontanus). Divides the Celestial Equator into twelve equal 15° hour-segments starting from the East Point, using great circles passing through the North and South poles of the horizon. Highly favored in traditional horary and electional astrology.

entries.section: 3. Quadrant Systems: Spatial / Great Circle Division
entries.text: An equatorial system designed by Jean-Baptiste Morin that divides the celestial equator into twelve 30° segments using poles of the ecliptic, creating houses that do not depend on terrestrial latitude.

The most widely used modern house system, popularized by 17th-century monk Placidus de Titis. A time-based system where intermediate cusps are calculated by trisecting the diurnal and nocturnal semi-arcs (planetary hours) traveled by zodiacal degrees as they rise from the horizon to the meridian. Highly sensitive for transits and predictive work, though it breaks down at extreme northern/southern latitudes above 66°.

Developed in the 20th century by Heinz Koch and Walter Specht. A time-based system that trisects the diurnal semi-arc of the Midheaven, projecting that motion backward to the horizon to define intermediate house cusps. Popular in modern psychological and predictive astrology.

A historical medieval system named after 10th-century Arabic astrologer Al-Qabisi. Calculates intermediate cusps by trisecting the arc of Right Ascension (or ascensional time) that the Ascendant degree traverses until it reaches the meridian Midheaven. The dominant system during the late Middle Ages and Renaissance.

Created in the 20th century by Wendel Polich and A.P. Nelson Page. A empirical refinement of Placidus that calculates house cusps using cone projections from the exact surface location (topocentric point) of the Earth rather than its geocentric center.
An ancient pre-Hellenistic 8-house system preceding the 12-house system, dividing the chart into eight sectors focused on life, money, siblings, parents, children, illness, spouse, and death.

An equatorial space system designed by L.G. Krafft that divides the celestial equator into twelve equal 30° arcs by lunes from the celestial poles, taking the Equatorial Ascendant as the 1st cusp and MC as the 10th cusp.

A simplified chart setup where the exact degree and sign of the natal Sun is placed on the 1st house cusp, with subsequent equal 30° sign arcs defining the remaining house cusps; used when exact birth time is unknown.
The exact mathematical boundary line marking the beginning of a house. Represents the point of maximum potency and concentration of energy for that house.
The cusps of the non-angular houses (Houses 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12) calculated between the four primary angles.
A classical interpretive rule stated by Ptolemy, where any planet falling within 5° (or up to 6°) before a house cusp is interpreted as being functionally active inside the following house.
A zodiac sign completely enclosed within a large house without appearing on either of its surrounding house cusps; occurs frequently in high-latitude quadrant charts.
A house completely contained within a wide zodiac sign, causing two consecutive house cusps to bear the same zodiac sign.
The planet that rules the zodiac sign residing on the cusp of a given house. Acts as the landlord or director of all activities occurring within that house.
The technique of reading houses relative to a primary house to evaluate specific external connections (e.g., the 2nd house from the 7th house = 8th house, governing the spouse's money).
Classical technique where the three triplicity rulers of the sign on a house cusp are evaluated sequentially to analyze three distinct phases of a native's life regarding that house's topics.
The temporary operational strength a planet gains based on its house placement (such as being angular or in its house of joy) rather than its sign placement.

The crucial distinction between using houses to determine what areas of life a planet governs (topical) versus using quadrant/equal overlays to measure how forcefully or energetically a planet can act (dynamic strength).
The intrinsic strength, virtue, or authority a planet acquires based on its specific zodiacal degree placement.

The primary zodiac sign(s) ruled by a planet (+5 scoring points). A planet in its domicile acts like a monarch or master in their own home or realm, possessing full authority, resources, and independence of action.

The classic division of planetary rulerships where the non-luminary traditional planets rule one diurnal/masculine sign (extroverted expression) and one nocturnal/feminine sign (introverted expression).

The second highest level of essential dignity (+4 scoring points). A planet in exaltation functions like an honored royal guest, prime minister, or celebrated dignitary—it is elevated, respected, and highly potent, though its actions remain dependent on the host ruler.

Precise, single degrees within the exaltation signs where a planet's exalted virtue reaches its absolute zenith:
• Sun: 19° Aries
• Moon: 3° Taurus
• Mercury: 15° Virgo
• Venus: 27° Pisces
• Mars: 28° Capricorn
• Jupiter: 15° Cancer
• Saturn: 21° Libra

Dignity assigned based on elemental affinity (+3 scoring points). Represents being among family, friends, or supportive kin. Three planets rule each triplicity in sequence: a Diurnal ruler (active in day charts), a Nocturnal ruler (active in night charts), and a Participating/Common ruler (providing steady baseline support):
• Fire Triplicity (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius): Sun (Day), Jupiter (Night), Saturn (Participating).
• Earth Triplicity (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn): Venus (Day), Moon (Night), Mars (Participating).
• Air Triplicity (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius): Saturn (Day), Mercury (Night), Jupiter (Participating).
• Water Triplicity (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces): Venus (Day), Mars (Night), Moon (Participating).

Five unequal subdivisions of each 30° zodiac sign ruled by the five traditional non-luminary planets (+2 scoring points). Functions as a planet's private "fiefdom" or specific behavioral limits; a planet in its own term acts according to its own rules and boundaries regardless of sign placement.
• Egyptian Terms: The most widely utilized classical table of bounds across Hellenistic, Arabic, and Medieval astrology.
• Ptolemaic Terms: An alternative system of terms formulated by Ptolemy in the Tetrabiblos.

Three equal 10° divisions per zodiac sign (+1 scoring point). Ruled sequentially by the descending Chaldean Order of planetary speed (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon). Represents the baseline, subtle level of essential dignity—a planet in its face has minimal authority, like someone maintaining basic decorum.

Placement in the zodiac sign directly opposite a planet's home domicile (-5 scoring points). Forces the planet to operate in a foreign, uncomfortable environment, twisting its natural virtues into corresponding defects (e.g., Saturn's sobriety turning into melancholy, or Jupiter's generosity turning into squandering).
Placement in the zodiac sign directly opposite a planet's exaltation (-4 scoring points). Characterized by clumsiness, instability, exaggeration, or feeling humbled and out of place.

The condition where a planet holds zero essential dignities (no domicile, exaltation, triplicity, term, or face) in its current degree. Acts like a landless wanderer or homeless traveler without ties or responsibilities, completely subject to its host dispositor (-5 points when unassisted).

A specific sign placement (distinct from domicile) where a planet's elemental temperament (hot, cold, wet, dry) is perfectly balanced and tempered by the sign's nature (e.g., Saturn in Aquarius, Mars in Scorpio, Mercury in Virgo).
Positioned between 8° (or 8.5°) and 12°–17° from the Sun. The planet's light is partially obscured by solar glare, causing mild weakening (-4 scoring points).

A severe accidental debility occurring when a planet is within 8° (or 8.5°) of the Sun. The planet's light is completely swallowed by solar heat and glare, burning away its independent strength and hiding its operations (-6 scoring points).

entries.term: Cazimi (In the Heart of the Sun / In Corde Solis)
entries.text: An exceptionally powerful accidental dignity occurring when a planet is within 17 minutes of arc (0°17') of the exact center of the Sun (+5 scoring points). Rather than being burned, the planet enters the royal inner sanctuary, receiving supreme illumination, authority, and audience with the king.
A planet positioned more than 16°–17° away from the Sun (+5 scoring points), allowing it to shine with full visibility in the night or morning sky.
The building (+1 point) or waning (-1 point) phase of a planet's or Moon's luminosity as it moves away from or toward conjunction with the Sun.
A superior planet (Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) that rises in the dawn sky before the Sun (+2 scoring points). Operates with forward drive, initiative, and active expression.
An inferior planet (Mercury, Venus) or Moon that sets in the twilight sky after the Sun (+2 scoring points). Operates with reflection, evaluation, and receptive processing.
Normal forward progression through the zodiac (+4 scoring points).
Apparent backward movement across the zodiac (-5 scoring points). Turns the planet's energy inward, delaying concrete outcomes, resisting standard norms, and forcing review or recalculation.
The exact pause in celestial longitude as a planet transitions between direct and retrograde motion. Concentrates planetary energy to a sharp, intense focal point.

entries.term: Fast in Speed (Swift in Course / Velocity)
entries.text: A planet traveling faster than its average daily orbital motion (+2 scoring points), accelerating events and bringing rapid results.
A planet traveling slower than its daily average (-2 scoring points), lingering in its effects and delaying outcomes.
The ruling planet that owns essential dignity (domicile, exaltation, etc.) over the degree occupied by another body, acting as its landlord.
A relationship where Planet A resides in a sign or dignity ruled by Planet B, and Planet B "receives" Planet A like a welcoming host receiving a guest into their home.
An exceptionally strong bond formed when two planets occupy each other's essential dignities (e.g., Sun in Aries and Mars in Leo, or Mercury in Capricorn and Saturn in Gemini) (+5 scoring points).
The transmission of power that occurs when a planet in its major dignities (domicile/exaltation) casts an aspect to another body, transferring its strength and assisting the receiving planet.
Occurs when a planet receives another body, but because the receiving planet is combust, retrograde, or cadent, it cannot hold the energy and "returns" the virtue back without fulfilling the promise.
A severe accidental debility where a planet is trapped directly between the bodies or exact applying aspects of the two malefics (Mars and Saturn) without benefic intervention (-5 scoring points).
An accidental dignity where a planet is enclosed or supported between the bodies or aspects of the two benefics (Venus and Jupiter) (+5 scoring points).
The foundational Hellenistic and Medieval division of charts into Diurnal (day births, Sun above horizon) and Nocturnal (night births, Sun below horizon) teams.

A composite accidental dignity (+3 scoring points) achieved when a planet satisfies three alignment conditions simultaneously:
1. Matches the chart's overall sect (diurnal planet in a day chart / nocturnal in a night chart).
2. Resides in the correct hemisphere relative to the Sun (diurnal planets above horizon with Sun / nocturnal below).
3. Resides in a sign matching its gender (diurnal/masculine planet in a masculine sign; nocturnal/feminine planet in a feminine sign).
The state where a planet violates all conditions of sect, hemisphere, and gender (-2 scoring points), causing discomfort and instability.
An extremely rare, supreme state of accidental dignity (+5 scoring points) where a planet is in Hayz, placed in an angular house, oriental to the Sun (in a day chart), and free from all afflictions.

The planet that accumulates the overall highest sum of calculated essential and accidental dignity points for a specific degree, house cusp, or for the entire horoscope (Almuten Figuris / Lord of the Geniture).
The angular distance measured in degrees along the ecliptic (or equator) between two celestial bodies or chart points, allowing their archetypal energies to interact.
The allowable margin of deviation (in degrees and minutes of arc) from an exact geometric aspect within which two planets are still considered functionally connected.
An aspect formed when a faster-moving planet is actively traveling toward an exact degree alignment with a slower planet, representing building energy, impending events, and future momentum.
An aspect formed as a faster-moving planet moves away from exact alignment with another body, representing receding conditions, past experiences, or established patterns.
An aspect that is exact to the same degree (0° orb), conferring maximum intensity, visibility, and immediate manifestation power.
An aspect that is not exact but falls within the accepted orb threshold, operating with a broader, more diffuse influence.
An aspect cast backward against the natural order of the signs (clockwise), associated with conscious willpower, self-projection, and direct action.
An aspect cast forward in the natural order of the signs (counter-clockwise), associated with receptive processing, social interaction, and external outcomes.
An aspect cast from a slower, heavier, or higher-ranking planet to a faster or lighter planet, where the superior body asserts dominance over the interaction.
An aspect cast from a faster, lighter planet up toward a superior planet, where the lighter planet adapts to the superior body's framework.

A major major aspect where two or more planets occupy the exact same degree or sign space. Blends their energies into a single concentrated impulse; can be benefic or challenging depending on the planets involved.

A major harmonious aspect connecting planets two signs apart in compatible elements (Fire/Air or Earth/Water). Creates mental stimulation, opportunities, communication, and pleasant flow that requires conscious activation.

A major dynamic aspect connecting planets three signs apart in the same modality (Cardinal, Fixed, or Mutable). Generates intense internal friction, structural challenge, and a powerful drive to take physical action and overcome obstacles.

A major flowing aspect connecting planets four signs apart in the exact same element. Grants innate talent, unearned luck, creative harmony, and effortless expression, though it can sometimes lead to complacency.
A major polar aspect connecting planets six signs apart directly across the chart. Brings objective awareness, relationship confrontation, tension, and the need to balance opposing life forces.
A minor aspect connecting adjacent signs. Creates subtle discomfort or awkwardness because adjacent signs share neither element nor modality, requiring conscious adjustment.
A minor hard aspect causing acute friction, irritation, and minor setbacks that prompt prompt problem-solving.
A minor harmonic aspect associated with specialized creative genius, technical skill, pattern recognition, and spiritual transformation.
A minor harmonic aspect representing highly developed artistic, mathematical, or esoteric talents that manifest through disciplined focus.
A minor hard aspect generating persistent agitation, stubborn obstacles, and external pressure to break through stagnant situations.
A major minor aspect connecting signs that share no polarity, element, or modality (e.g., Aries and Virgo). Demands continuous adaptation, psychological realignment, and health/lifestyle adjustments.
An esoteric harmonic aspect associated with non-rational understanding, divine inspiration, fated turning points, and mystical calling.
A spiritual aspect associated with inner realization, karmic initiation, processing emotional lessons, and spiritual digestion.
An aspect formed when two planets share the exact same degree of declination north or south of the celestial equator; operates with the strength and blending power of a conjunction.
An aspect formed when two planets occupy the exact same degree of declination on opposite sides of the celestial equator (one North, one South); operates with the balancing tension of an opposition.
Squares, Oppositions, Semi-Squares, and Sesquiquadrates. Energies that demand effort, provoke growth, build strength, and compel physical manifestation.
Trines, Sextiles, and Quintiles. Energies that integrate smoothly, promote relaxation, foster inherent abilities, and minimize resistance.

An aspect where the geometric distance meets the degree requirement, but the planets reside in signs that do not match the standard aspect relationship (e.g., a planet at 29° Aries trine a planet at 1° Virgo). Creates unusual, hybrid psychological dynamics.

A planet that forms no major Ptolemaic aspects to any other planet in the chart. Acts as an isolated "wild card," fluctuating between feeling dormant and operating with unchanneled, pure archetype intensity.
A single planet that stands alone in an entire hemisphere, element, or modality, drawing an immense amount of the chart's focal energy toward itself.

A classical mechanism where a fast planet (often the Moon) separates from an aspect with Planet A and immediately applies to an aspect with Planet B, carrying the energy of A to B and bringing about a resolution between them.

Occurs when two heavy planets do not aspect each other directly, but both apply to aspects with a third, slower planet in a dominant position, which "collects" their energies and brings them to fruition.
Occurs when two planets are applying toward an exact aspect, but a third, faster planet intervenes and forms an exact aspect first, preventing or "cutting off" the original event.

A concentration of three (or traditionally four) or more planets in a single sign or house. Creates an intense focal point of energy, driving personality traits and life themes heavily into that area.

A closed equilateral triangle formed by three planets spaced ~120° apart, usually all in the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water). Represents a closed circuit of innate talent, self-containment, and effortless creative flow.

A dynamic pattern formed by two planets in an opposition, both casting 90° squares to a third "Apex" (or Focal) planet. Generates intense stress and ambition, with the Apex planet acting as the primary outlet for action.

A powerful pattern formed by four planets making four squares and two oppositions across the entire chart, involving all four signs of a single modality (Cardinal, Fixed, or Mutable). Creates immense internal drive, life challenges, and monumental capacity for achievement.

An isosceles triangle formed by two planets in a 60° sextile, both casting 150° quincunx aspects to a third "Apex" planet. Indicates a spiritual turning point, a feeling of destiny, and a requirement to make continual adjustments to fulfill a unique calling.

A Yod configuration that includes a fourth planet positioned directly opposite the Apex planet (in the midpoint of the sextile base), providing an external anchor and clear release valve for the Yod's tension.

Formed when a Grand Trine is augmented by a fourth planet that opposes one of the trine points and forms sextiles to the other two. The opposing planet acts as a "tail" or rudder, providing the motivation and practical drive to utilize the Grand Trine's natural talents.

A harmonious configuration formed by four planets linked by two trines, two sextiles, and two oppositions. Combines deep creative talent with the practical tension necessary to manifest ideas in the real world.
Formed by four planets linked by three sextiles, two quarters, and a baseline opposition spanning one hemisphere. Acts as a protective "safety net," offering refuge during personal crises.
Formed by two planets in a 90° square, both casting 135° sesquiquadrate aspects to a third Apex planet. Creates sharp, disruptive tension aimed at dismantling outdated structures.
An exceptionally rare configuration formed by five planets spaced ~72° apart, creating a five-pointed star of creative genius, extraordinary pattern recognition, and cosmic alignment.
A rare configuration formed by six planets making two intertwined Grand Trines connected by six sextiles. Creates a complete, balanced interdimensional resonator of energy and talent.
The primary cross of matter formed by the local Horizon (Ascendant/Descendant) and Meridian (Midheaven/Imum Coeli).
The horizontal axis dividing the chart into upper (public) and lower (private) hemispheres. Measures self-awareness (ASC) versus relationship awareness (DSC).

entries.term: Midheaven / Imum Coeli Axis (Developmental Meridian Axis)
entries.text: The vertical axis dividing the chart into eastern (self-determined) and western (other-oriented) hemispheres. Measures psychological roots/ancestry (IC) versus public vocation/standing (MC).
The intersection of the Prime Vertical with the Ecliptic in the west (Vertex) and east (Antivertex). Acts as an auxiliary relational axis triggering fated encounters and turning points.
The point where the celestial equator intersects the eastern horizon; used in specialized directional and location astrology.
The degree of the ecliptic located exactly 90° from the Ascendant, marking the absolute highest spatial arc of the ecliptic above the horizon at any given moment.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: A distribution where all ten planets are evenly scattered around the 360° zodiac wheel, occupying at least eight to ten signs with no gap between adjacent planets exceeding ~60°. Represents a versatile, Gemini-like temperament with broad interests, varied talents, and an ability to relate to many fields, though caution is required to prevent scattering energy without direction. Associated with the planet Mercury.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: An extreme concentration where all ten planets are tightly gathered within a single trine span of 120° (or up to 130°), leaving two-thirds (240°) of the chart completely empty. Represents an intense, specialized focus, narrow interests, and high self-reliance, operating as a dedicated expert or specialist who works from limited initial resources. Associated with the planet Saturn.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: A pattern where all ten planets are contained within one half of the horoscope (180° to 190°), bounded by an opposition across its rim, leaving the opposite 180° empty. Represents a self-contained, focused personality who collects experiences in the occupied arc while feeling an underlying challenge or compulsion to achieve in the empty hemisphere. Associated with the Moon.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: A pattern where planets span two-thirds of the chart (240°), leaving an empty trine segment of 120°. Driven by the "Leading Planet" (the planet at the front edge of the 240° arc moving clockwise), it represents dynamic drive, executive capability, self-motivation, and a persistent urge to conquer the area of life represented by the empty trine. Associated with Mars.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: A pattern where nine planets form a Bowl or Bundle in one hemisphere, while a single isolated planet (or tight conjunction) stands alone in the opposite hemisphere to act as the "Handle" or "Singleton". The lone handle planet acts as the primary release valve, catalyst, and focal outlet for the entire energy stored within the bowl. Associated with Jupiter.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: A biform configuration where planets are divided into two distinct opposing groups separated by two empty areas of at least 60° (or empty squares) on either side. Represents a Libra-like temperament characterized by weighing opposing perspectives, wrestling with dualities, mediating conflicts, and seeking internal balance between two contrasting life arenas. Associated with Venus.

entries.section: The Classic Marc Edmund Jones Planetary Patterns (Core Seven Shapes)
entries.text: A triform distribution where planets are grouped into three distinct, sharp clusters or "spokes" separated by empty spaces, often forming a Grand Trine or T-Square framework. Represents a fiercely individualistic, unconventional personality who resists conformity, operates on their own terms, and grounds disparate energies through three firm anchor points. Associated with the Sun.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: A biform variation of the Bucket where nine planets are tightly packed into a 120° Bundle (rather than a 180° Bowl), with a single planet standing opposite as the handle. The singleton handle acts as a powerful "cause" or driver directing the entire momentum of the Bundle.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: An ultra-condensed Bucket variation where nine planets are compressed within 120°, and the singleton handle stands opposite at least 60° away from the boundary planets. Indicates a resolute, pugnacious individual with a "David and Goliath" determination to conquer monumental tasks.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: A Bucket variation where the handle consists of two planets in a tight conjunction in the opposite hemisphere, pooling two distinct archetypal energies into the primary focal outlet.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: A Bucket variation where two separate, un-conjoined planets reside in the opposite hemisphere, creating two distinct parallel or consecutive channels of life focus.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: Specific symmetrical manifestations of the Seesaw pattern where the opposing groups are tightly grouped like an hourglass or flared like butterfly wings.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: Jansky's mathematical formulation of the Splay pattern, requiring three distinct planetary clusters anchored by exact trines between the groups.

entries.section: Structural Variations & Sub-Types (Jansky, McEvers & Modern Extensions)
entries.text: A triform pattern discovered by Jansky and March consisting of a tight Bundle body (contained within a trine or square) flanked by two singleton handles on either side, requiring careful balancing of life loads.

The primary focal planet that serves as the starting point for delineating a chart shape (e.g., the handle of a Bucket, the engine of a Locomotive, or the fastest mover in a core opposition). Represents the primary modus operandi and driving engine of the personality.

In a Locomotive, Bowl, or Bundle, the first planet encountered when moving counter-clockwise from the empty space into the occupied arc. Acts as the front-runner, initiating willpower, energy, and drive.
The last planet at the rear edge of a planetary grouping moving counter-clockwise. Represents how projects end, the background support structure, or the stabilizing anchor behind the leading edge.
A solitary planet residing alone in an entire hemisphere or quadrant, carrying the weight of the opposite planetary cluster and acting as the main channel of self-expression.

The two outer edge planets that bound the occupied arc of a pattern (such as the two rim planets of a Bowl or Bundle). Their essential nature, aspects, and midpoints define the primary boundary conditions of the native's life.
The exact mathematical midpoint between the two boundary planets. A sensitive point whose house and sign placement—and any planet occupying it—reveal the core integration axis of the chart.

The empty segment of the zodiac containing no planets (e.g., the 120° empty arc in a Locomotive or the 180° empty arc in a Bowl). Symbolizes unfamiliar territory, latent hunger, or the external shadow area that the native seeks to integrate.
A planet that resides in its own domicile and ultimately rules all other planets through a chain of dispositorship, acting as the ultimate authority of the chart.
A planet that serves as the unique link or bridge between two distinct aspect configurations (e.g., a planet sitting at the apex of a T-Square that also forms one corner of a Grand Trine).

A concentration of planets on the left side of the chart surrounding the Ascendant. Indicates a self-determined, action-oriented individual who molds circumstances, takes direct initiative, and maintains personal control over their destiny.

A concentration of planets on the right side of the chart surrounding the Descendant. Indicates an other-directed, responsive individual whose life path is heavily molded by circumstances, relationships, and collaboration with others.

A concentration of planets below the horizon. Indicates an introspective, private individual motivated by inner goals, personal foundation, family, and subjective self-mastery rather than public acclaim.

A concentration of planets above the horizon. Indicates an extroverted, career-oriented individual focused on outer achievement, public standing, social contribution, and objective worldly engagement.
Focus on subjective self-discovery, physical emergence, personal awareness, and establishing core identity.
Focus on organic growth, subjective creativity, self-expression, personal security, and honing practical skills.
Focus on objective relationship processing, social awareness, partnerships, legal ties, and expanding philosophical horizons.
Focus on public integration, professional mastery, collective contribution, institutional leadership, and universal consciousness.

The numerical tally of planets across Fire, Earth, Air, and Water signs. Measures whether the native leads through intuition/inspiration (Fire), practical realism (Earth), intellect/logic (Air), or emotional depth (Water).

The numerical tally of planets across Cardinal, Fixed, and Mutable modes. Measures whether the native's operational style is driving/initiating (Cardinal), persistent/stabilizing (Fixed), or adaptable/flexible (Mutable).

The complete absence of planets in a specific element or modality (e.g., zero planets in Water or zero in Fixed signs). Creates an intense psychological compensation drive, where the individual over-emphasizes or compulsively seeks out that missing quality in external life.
Possessing five or more planets in a single element or modality, creating an overwhelming concentration of that specific temperament.
The composite sign archetype derived by combining the single most dominant Element with the most dominant Modality in the chart (e.g., dominant Fixed + dominant Water = a Scorpio signature).

entries.section: Foundational Hermetic Mechanics & Rules of Calculation
entries.text: A sensitive degree on the ecliptic derived by measuring the arc distance between two celestial bodies (or points) and projecting that exact distance from a third anchor point (almost always the Ascendant).

entries.section: Foundational Hermetic Mechanics & Rules of Calculation
entries.text: The classical requirement to reverse the direction of the calculation arc depending on whether the chart is a Diurnal birth (Sun above the horizon) or a Nocturnal birth (Sun below the horizon). Reversing the formula preserves the proper mathematical relationship between the light and shadow forces.

entries.section: Foundational Hermetic Mechanics & Rules of Calculation
entries.text: The point from which the measured arc is projected across the chart wheel. In over 90% of traditional Lots, the Ascendant acts as the universal physical anchor.

entries.section: Foundational Hermetic Mechanics & Rules of Calculation
entries.text: The planet that owns essential dignity (domicile/rulership) over the zodiac sign where a Lot falls. The condition, placement, and aspects of the Lot's ruler determine whether the promise of the Lot manifests in physical reality.

entries.section: Foundational Hermetic Mechanics & Rules of Calculation
entries.text: A ancient predictive time-lord technique that uses the Lots of Fortune and Spirit as dynamic time engines. Planetary periods unfold through the zodiac signs starting from the Lot, unlocking major chapters of physical health (Fortune) or career/calling (Spirit).

entries.section: Foundational Hermetic Mechanics & Rules of Calculation
entries.text: The longitudinal distance measured clockwise or counter-clockwise along the ecliptic to determine the exact degree length of a Lot formula.

• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Sun - Moon
• Meaning: Governs the physical body, health, material circumstances, spontaneous fortune, physical environment, and unearned worldly events.

• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Sun - Moon
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Moon - Sun
• Meaning: Governs the soul, mind, intellect, intentional choice, career initiative, moral purpose, and actions taken through conscious willpower.

• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Lot of Spirit - Venus (Variant: ASC + Fortune - Venus)

• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Mercury - Lot of Fortune
• Meaning: Governs constraints, unavoidable circumstances, physical struggles, legal subordinations, enmities, and fate.

• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Mars - Lot of Fortune
• Meaning: Governs physical boldness, risk-taking, martial energy, physical strength, impulse, and heroic or reckless action.

• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Jupiter - Lot of Spirit
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Lot of Spirit - Jupiter
• Meaning: Governs faith, good hope, successful resolution, expansion, legal triumph, enterprise, and divine assistance.

• Meaning: Governs hidden obstacles, structural weakness, retributive justice, exile, loss, sickness, and karmic boundaries.

entries.text:

• Meaning: Reveals the underlying physical and spiritual foundation of the horoscope, indicating baseline stability and potential for public eminence.

entries.text:
