entries.section: Major Medieval & Arabic Relational & Personal Lots
entries.text:
• Formula: ASC + Saturn - Venus (or ASC + Moon - Mars).
• Meaning: Evaluates the timing, nature, and conditions of marital partnerships for a female native.

entries.section: Major Medieval & Arabic Relational & Personal Lots
entries.text:
• Formula: ASC + Saturn - Jupiter (Diurnal) / ASC + Jupiter - Saturn (Nocturnal).
• Meaning: Indicates fertility, offspring, creative legacy, and relationships with children.

entries.section: Major Medieval & Arabic Relational & Personal Lots
entries.text:
• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Saturn - Sun
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Sun - Saturn
• Meaning: Governs the father's health, social standing, relationship with the native, and paternal inheritance.

entries.section: Major Medieval & Arabic Relational & Personal Lots
entries.text:
• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Venus - Moon
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Moon - Venus
• Meaning: Governs the mother's longevity, maternal nurturing, ancestral ties, and relationship with the native.

entries.section: Major Medieval & Arabic Relational & Personal Lots
entries.text:
• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Jupiter - Saturn
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Saturn - Jupiter
• Meaning: Reveals relationships with brothers, sisters, and close extended family kin.

• Formula: ASC + Mercury - Sun.
• Meaning: Governs business transactions, mercantile skill, contract negotiations, and financial exchanges.

entries.term: Lot of Possessions / Wealth (Substance / 2nd House Lot)
entries.text:
• Formula: ASC + 2nd Cusp - Ruler of 2nd House (or ASC + Moon - Ruler of 2nd).
• Meaning: Pinpoints earned liquid wealth, material assets, personal savings, and financial security.

entries.term: Lot of Real Estate / Property (Assets & Ancestral Lands)
entries.text:
• Formula: ASC + Saturn - Moon.
• Meaning: Governs physical real estate, land ownership, buildings, farming, and underground wealth.

• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Moon - Saturn
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Saturn - Moon
• Meaning: Pinpoints career calling, social position, professional domain, and life's primary work output.

• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Sun - Jupiter
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Jupiter - Sun
• Meaning: Governs public recognition, social prestige, high honor, awards, and rise in status.

• Formula: ASC + 8th Cusp - Moon.
• Meaning: Used in traditional longevity analysis to evaluate physical end-of-life conditions and major structural transitions.

• Diurnal Formula: ASC + Saturn - Mars
• Nocturnal Formula: ASC + Mars - Saturn
• Meaning: Pinpoints bodily vulnerabilities, surgical intervention, physical trauma, or legal accusations.

• Formula: ASC + Ruler of 12th - 12th Cusp (or ASC + Saturn - Ruler of 12th).
• Meaning: Governs clandestine plots, hidden adversaries, confinement, exile, and self-sabotage.

entries.term: Lot of Flight / Exile / Unexcused Absence
entries.text:
• Formula: ASC + Mercury - Moon.
• Meaning: Pinpoints periods of fleeing danger, forced displacement, exile, or wandering away from home.
The specific planet or chart point (Sun, Moon, ASC, Lot of Fortune, or Syzygy) that holds primary authority over physical vitality and longevity.
The malefic planet or directional point that forms an exact aspect or alignment to the Hyleg, signifying physical crisis or the termination of life.
The exact mathematical middle degree ((Planet A + Planet B)/2) between any two planets or angles (e.g., Sun/Moon Midpoint representing core personality integration).
The astronomical intersection of the Prime Vertical with the Ecliptic on the western (Vertex) and eastern (Antivertex) horizons; acts as a sensitive relationship and turning-point axis.
The degree of the ecliptic that rises at the intersection of the celestial equator and the eastern horizon; used as an auxiliary Ascendant.

The exact degree of the last New Moon (SAN - Sanctum Alignment) or Full Moon (SAF) occurring immediately prior to birth. Serves as a vital anchor point for bodily incarnation and longevity calculations.
A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign. Because each of the 12 signs spans 30°, there are exactly 3 decans per sign, totaling 36 decans across the entire 360° zodiac wheel.

The historical origin of the decans, dating back to 2nd millennium BCE Egypt. Originally 36 stellar asterisms that rose sequentially over the eastern horizon throughout the night to mark the passage of time and the 10-day Egyptian "weeks".

The traditional Hellenistic, Arabic, and Medieval term for a decan when evaluated as a planetary subdivision. A planet residing in its own face receives +1 point of essential dignity in traditional scoring tables.

The ancient descending order of planetary speed and proximity to Earth based on the geocentric model: Saturn → Jupiter → Mars → Sun → Venus → Mercury → Moon. This sequence governs the planetary rulership of the 36 faces, planetary hours, and days of the week.
A secondary planetary ruler assigned to govern a specific 10° decan, acting alongside the primary sign ruler to refine the nuance and behavior of a natal placement.

A 10-degree subdivision of a 30-degree zodiac sign. Because there are 12 signs in the zodiac, the 360° celestial wheel is divided into exactly 36 decans.

The astronomical origin of the decans. Long before they were merged with the 12 zodiac signs, early Egyptian astronomers tracked 36 fixed star asterisms that rose sequentially across the night sky, dividing the year into 36 ten-day "weeks" or seasonal periods.

The traditional Hellenistic, Arabic, and Medieval term for a decan when evaluated as a planetary subdivision. Placing a planet in its own face grants it a baseline level of essential dignity (+1 point in traditional scoring systems).
The traditional geocentric sequence of the seven visible planets arranged by relative orbital speed and proximity to Earth: Saturn → Jupiter → Mars → Sun → Venus → Mercury → Moon.

A distinct Hellenistic doctrine described by Ptolemy and Porphyry that should not be confused with decans. A planet is in its "proper face" when it holds the same phase relationship to the Sun or Moon that it holds in the Thema Mundi (e.g., Venus being two signs away from the Sun).
A secondary planetary ruler assigned to govern a specific 10° decan, modifying and refining the expression of a planet residing in that decanate.

The traditional system of 28 lunar stations codified by medieval Islamic astrologers and later transmitted to Renaissance Europe through the Picatrix.
Standardized 12°51'26" segments (exactly (360°)/28) anchored to 0° Aries (the Vernal Equinox). This system forms the primary basis of medieval electional astrology and talismanic magic.

The historical, irregular mansions defined directly by physical star markers (such as Aldebaran, Spica, and Antares). Due to axial precession (~1° every 72 years), the physical indicator stars slowly drift relative to the tropical boundaries.
The 28 mansions divide into four equal sets of seven mansions. Each set of seven mansions corresponds to one season and spans three solar zodiac signs.
The practice of timing actions, journeys, treaties, or talismanic carving to coincide with the Moon's passage through specific auspicious mansions.

entries.term: 1. Al-Sharatain ("The Two Signals / Horns of Aries")
entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 0°00' Aries – 12°51' Aries.
Indicator Stars: Beta Arietis (Sheratan) and Gamma Arietis (Mesarthim).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Geniel (Agrippa) / Gabriel (Picatrix).
Essential Nature & Elections: Highly fiery, energetic, and martial. Auspicious for undertaking journeys, riding, and taking medicine; inauspicious for marriage or close personal friendships due to excessive heat.
Talismanic Image: A standing armed warrior holding a spear and shield.

entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 12°51' Aries – 25°43' Aries.
Indicator Stars: Delta and Epsilon Arietis.
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Enediel (Agrippa) / Geliel.
Essential Nature & Elections: Grounding, stabilizing, and resource-oriented. Excellent for discovering hidden treasures, retaining captives, and joining what was separated.
Talismanic Image: A king or crowned figure holding a scepter.

entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 25°43' Aries – 8°34' Taurus.
Indicator Stars: Eta Tauri (Alcyone / The Pleiades cluster).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Amixiel (Agrippa) / Azoraye.
Essential Nature & Elections: Favorable for alchemists, sailors, huntsmen, and scientific study. Good for planting and sowing, but inauspicious for sea travel or marriage.
Talismanic Image: A seated woman with her right hand raised above her head.

entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 8°34' Taurus – 21°26' Taurus.
Indicator Star: Alpha Tauri (Aldebaran).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Azariel (Agrippa) / Aldebaram.
Essential Nature & Elections: Severe, destructive, and combative (of Mars nature). Causes destruction of buildings, gold mines, and wells, and prompts discord. Used in magic for binding enemies.
Talismanic Image: A horseman carrying a serpent in his right hand.

entries.term: 5. Al-Haqa ("The White Spot / Head of Orion")
entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 21°26' Taurus – 4°17' Gemini.
Indicator Star: Lambda Orionis (Meissa).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Gabiel (Agrippa) / Almices.
Essential Nature & Elections: Intellectual, noble, and governing. Excellent for instruction, return from travel, health, goodwill, and receiving favors from superiors.
Talismanic Image: A crowned head without a body.

entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 4°17' Gemini – 17°09' Gemini.
Indicator Star: Gamma Geminorum (Alhena).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Dirach (Agrippa) / Athaya.
Essential Nature & Elections: Dual nature; favorable for hunting, besieging, and royal retribution, but destructive to harvests and medical treatments. Favorable for love when guided by Saturnian gravity.
Talismanic Image: Two figures embracing or a man wrapped in robes.

entries.section: Quarter I: Vernal Mansions (Aries, Taurus, Gemini)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 17°09' Gemini – 0°00' Cancer.
Indicator Stars: Alpha (Castor) and Beta (Pollux) Geminorum.
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Scheliel (Agrippa) / Selehe.
Essential Nature & Elections: Highly benefic and abundant. Increases trade, profits, crops, and safe sea navigation, while fostering lasting friendship between allies.
Talismanic Image: A man robed in white with hands extended toward heaven in prayer.

entries.term: 8. Al-Nathrah ("The Gap / Crib / Nose of Leo")
entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 0°00' Cancer – 12°51' Cancer.
Indicator Star: 44 M Cancri (Praesepe / The Beehive Cluster).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Amnediel (Agrippa) / Annediex.
Essential Nature & Elections: Victorious and triumphant. Promotes love, friendship, society among travelers, and triumph in battles or lawsuits.
Talismanic Image: An eagle with the face and head of a man.

entries.term: 9. Al-Tarf ("The Glance / Eyes of the Lion")
entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 12°51' Cancer – 25°43' Cancer.
Indicator Star: Lambda Leonis (Alterf).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Barbiel (Agrippa) / Archaam.
Essential Nature & Elections: Severe, restrictive, and disempowering. Causes infirmity, frustration, discord, and hindrance to travelers and harvests.
Talismanic Image: A man covering his eyes with both hands.

entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 25°43' Cancer – 8°34' Leo.
Indicator Stars: Alpha Leonis (Regulus), Zeta, and Eta Leonis.
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Ardesiel (Agrippa) / Aredafir.
Essential Nature & Elections: Regal, therapeutic, and protective. Strengthens buildings, fosters love and benevolence, cures physical infirmity, and aids against enemies.
Talismanic Image: The head and mane of a roaring lion.

entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 8°34' Leo – 21°26' Leo.
Indicator Stars: Delta Leonis (Zosma) and Theta Leonis (Coxa).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Neciel (Agrippa) / Azobra.
Essential Nature & Elections: Dominant, authoritative, and prestigious. Favorable for voyages, mercantile gain, releasing captives, and establishing lordship.
Talismanic Image: A warrior riding a lion, holding a spear in his right hand and the lion's ear in his left.

entries.term: 12. Al-Sarfah ("The Changer of Weather / Tail of Leo")
entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 21°26' Leo – 4°17' Virgo.
Indicator Star: Beta Leonis (Denebola).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Abdizuel (Agrippa) / Alzarpha.
Essential Nature & Elections: Combative, transformative, and separating. Favorable for agriculture and improving servants, but causes strife, separation in love, and destruction to ships.
Talismanic Image: A man fighting a long, sinuous dragon.

entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 4°17' Virgo – 17°09' Virgo.
Indicator Stars: Beta, Eta, Gamma, Delta, and Epsilon Virginis.
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Jazeriel (Agrippa) / Azerut.
Essential Nature & Elections: Erotic, binding, and prosperous. Increases trade, harvests, and safe travel, and dissolves sexual impotence or relational distance between lovers.
Talismanic Image: Two figures (man and woman) bound in an intimate embrace.

entries.section: Quarter II: Aestival Mansions (Cancer, Leo, Virgo)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 17°09' Virgo – 0°00' Libra.
Indicator Star: Alpha Virginis (Spica).
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Ergediel (Agrippa) / Azimeth.
Essential Nature & Elections: Healing, harmonious, and marital. Cures sickness, fosters marital love, and aids sailors, but hinders land journeys.
Talismanic Image: A dog biting its own tail or a robed figure holding a sheaf of wheat.

entries.section: Quarter III: Autumnal Mansions (Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 0°00' Libra – 12°51' Libra.
Indicator Stars: Iota and Kappa Virginis.
Angel / Ruling Intelligence: Ataliel (Agrippa) / Algarpha.
Essential Nature & Elections: Clandestine, subterranean, and discordant. Favorable for digging wells, extracting buried treasure, and causing divorce or defeat of enemies.
Talismanic Image: A seated figure holding a scroll or shovel.

entries.section: Quarter III: Autumnal Mansions (Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius)
entries.text:
Tropical Span: 12°51' Libra – 25°43' Libra.
Indicator Stars: Alpha Librae (Zuben Elgenubi) and Beta Librae (Zuben Elakrab).

One 360th part of the celestial zodiac circle. Each of the twelve zodiac signs contains exactly 30 degrees (numbered 0°00'00" to 29°59'59").
The sexagesimal subdivisions of a degree. 1 degree = 60 minutes of arc; 1 minute = 60 seconds of arc.

The absolute final degree (29°00'00" to 29°59'59") of any sign. Represents a crisis threshold, an urgency to master that sign's evolutionary lessons, karmic completion, or a feeling of being at a major crossroads.
The initial degree (0°00'00" to 0°59'59") of a sign. Represents pure, unconditioned, raw energy emerging into new territory, operating with uninhibited momentum.

Specific degrees within signs derived from the 28 Lunar Mansions (roughly every 12°51') or classical sign divisions that carry heightened sensitivity and crisis potential:
• Cardinal Signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn): 0°, 13°, and 26°.
• Fixed Signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius): 8°–9° and 21°–22°.
• Mutable Signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces): 4° and 17°.

entries.term: Avatar Degrees (The Gateways of Power / 15° Fixed)
entries.text: The exact middle degree (15°) of the four Fixed signs (15° Taurus, 15° Leo, 15° Scorpio, 15° Aquarius). Associated with the four Cherubim or Sacred Beasts of Ezekiel's vision (Bull, Lion, Eagle, Human), acting as major focal points for releasing concentrated planetary power into physical form.
The two exact points where the celestial equator intersects the ecliptic. 0° Aries (Aries Point) marks the global public stage, worldly emergence, and universal visibility.
The maximum northern and southern declination limits of the Sun, marking major seasonal pivots and ancestral/institutional pillars.
An ancient Hellenistic system where every single degree of a sign is assigned a specific planetary ruler in Chaldean order, providing a micro-ruler for every individual degree.
A set of 360 symbolic images and poetic phrases corresponding to every single degree of the zodiac wheel.

The mandatory mathematical rule for reading Sabian Symbols. Because a degree represents an entire 60-minute space, any planet placed between 0°00'01" and 0°59'59" is operating within the 1st degree arc. Therefore, you always round UP to the next whole number (e.g., a planet at 14°02' Scorpio is read using the Sabian Symbol for 15° Scorpio).
The gifted crippled medium who channeled the 360 individual symbolic scenes in a single day using a shuffled deck of blank index cards.
*: The landmark 20th-century psychological and spiritual reinterpretation of the Sabian Symbols, structuring them as a 360-phase evolutionary journey of human consciousness.
The modern definitive work on Sabian Symbols, introducing practical keywords, action steps, cautions, and oracle mechanics for degree interpretation.
Alternative degree-symbolism systems (such as the Charubel degrees or the Chandra symbols channeled by John Sandbach) that offer parallel intuitive imagery for the 360 degrees.

The ancient, astronomically exact method of evaluating fixed stars pioneered by 1st-century astrologer Anonymous of 379 and modernized by Bernadette Brady. Occurs when a fixed star rises, culminates, sets, or anti-culminates on an angle at the exact same moment a planet reaches an angle, regardless of the star's ecliptic longitude.
The standard modern software method of projecting a star's location straight down onto the ecliptic line to measure conjunctions by degree longitude.

Fixed stars do not cast aspects (squares, trines, etc.); they operate almost exclusively through direct conjunctions or parallels. Because stars are distant points of light, standard orbs are tight:
• Ordinary Stars: 1° to 1.5° orb.
• Major First-Magnitude & Royal Stars: Up to 2° or 2.5° orb (especially when conjoined the Sun, Moon, or Ascendant).

Because of Earth's axial precession, fixed star positions drift forward through the tropical zodiac at a rate of approximately 50.26 seconds of arc per year (1 full degree every 71.6 years). Consequently, a star's tropical degree changes across centuries (e.g., Regulus entered tropical Virgo in late 2011/2012 after spending ~2,160 years in Leo).
Ptolemy's method of classifying the nature and color of fixed stars by comparing their visual light to pairs of planets (e.g., a star of "Jupiter/Mars nature" acts with expanding martial energy).

A classical predictive system that rotates the entire celestial sphere along the equator through diurnal motion, directing a natal body or house cusp (Significator) toward the exact place or aspect of another body or point (Promissor).
The natal point or planet that remains fixed in its local space concept while waiting to receive the directional arc of a moving body (e.g., the Ascendant, Midheaven, Sun, or Moon).
The planet, star, or point whose position is directed toward the Significator to promise or deliver a specific life event.
The classic mathematical equivalence where 1 degree of Right Ascension (or Oblique Ascension) along the celestial equator represents exactly 1 solar year of life.
A refined directional rate developed by Valentin Naibod based on the mean daily motion of the Sun in RA (59 minutes and 8 seconds of arc per year).

The primary directional method popularized by Placidus de Titis, which directs planets proportionally along their diurnal or nocturnal semi-arcs through the houses rather than purely along the ecliptic.
The degree of the celestial equator that rises (OA) or sets (OD) simultaneously with a given degree of the ecliptic at a specific terrestrial latitude; crucial for directing points to the horizon.
Directing a Significator or Promissor backward against the natural order of diurnal motion (into the quadrant prior to birth) to evaluate ancestral, prenatal, or deeply ingrained karmic patterns.
Moving celestial bodies forward in the natural direction of Earth's diurnal rotation.
Directions calculated strictly within the local house frame (using proportional house semi-arcs) regardless of zodiacal longitude.
Directions measured along the ecliptic where the promissor's longitude or aspect is projected onto the celestial equator to calculate the arc of direction.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: A symbolic time system based on the formula introduced scripturally (Ezekiel 4:6) and popularized in the 17th century by Placidus de Titis, where 1 day of planetary motion after birth equals 1 year of life.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: The fundamental distinction where transits occur in real physical time, whereas progressions operate within symbolic internal time, acting as the "soul's diary" and tracking the inner ripening of consciousness.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: A 29.5-year developmental cycle formed by the secondary progressed Sun and secondary progressed Moon. It replicates the 8 solar-lunar phases (New, Crescent, First Quarter, Gibbous, Full, Disseminating, Last Quarter, Balsamic) over ~30 years, marking major 3-to-4-year life chapters.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: The exact conjunction of the secondary progressed Moon with the secondary progressed Sun, occurring every 29.5 years. Marks an absolute structural rebirth, a clearing of the emotional decks, and the inception of a brand-new 30-year life chapter.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: The secondary progressed Moon opposing the progressed Sun (~14–15 years after the Progressed New Moon), bringing the peak realization, fulfillment, or illumination of the cycle's potential.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: The fastest-moving progressed body, traveling roughly 1 degree per month (~13° per year). It takes 27 to 29 years to make a complete circuit around the natal chart wheel, acting as the primary internal timer for emotional shifts and house emphasis.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: Advances at the rate of ~1 degree per year. Over a standard human lifespan, the Sun will progress through two to four zodiac signs, signaling major evolutionary shifts in core identity, ego strength, and creative vitality.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: The critical years when a secondary progressed inner planet (Mercury, Venus, or Mars) turns Stationary Retrograde or Stationary Direct. Signals a profound shift in mental processing (Mercury), relational values (Venus), or personal assertion (Mars).

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: The exact year when a secondary progressed planet or angle crosses the threshold into a new zodiac sign or house, shifting its underlying motivation and environmental flavor.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: A progressive variation that recalculates the exact primary angles (Ascendant and Midheaven) for the specific time of day corresponding to the progressed date, causing the angles to rotate through the wheel each year.

entries.section: Secondary Progressions ("Symbolic Time & The Soul's Diary")
entries.text: Measuring planetary movements in the ephemeris backward in time prior to birth (1 day before birth = 1 year of life) to evaluate deep-seated instinctual, ancestral, or karmic conditioning.
A directional system where the exact arc distance traveled by the secondary progressed Sun (approximately 1° per year) is added uniformly to every planet, asteroid, and angle in the natal chart.

Unlike secondary progressions where planets move at their own varying speeds, solar arcs move the entire chart as an interconnected, rigid framework. Therefore, all natal aspect angles (squares, trines, oppositions) are permanently preserved within the directed wheel.
The average daily distance the Sun travels along the ecliptic, creating the standard ~1° per year directional pace.

entries.term: Hard Aspect Focus in Solar Arcs
entries.text: Solar arcs operate with stark, event-oriented precision. Astrologers primarily evaluate hard aspects—Conjunctions (0°), Oppositions (180°), Squares (90°), Semi-Squares (45°), and Sesquiquadrates (135°)—to natal points and midpoints.

The practice popularized by Reinhold Ebertin and Cosmobiology, where solar arc directed planets form 45° or 90° contacts to natal planetary midpoints (e.g., Solar Arc Sun = Saturn/Pluto midpoint), triggering specific events.
Advancing the Ascendant and Midheaven by the Naibod rate (59'08" per year) rather than adding the true solar arc, ensuring smooth equatorial alignment.
Specialty directional systems that advance all planets by an arc defined by another body (e.g., Lunar Arc Directions, which advance the chart by the arc of the progressed Moon).
A specific planet activated by a timing technique to govern a particular chapter or sub-period of life. Transits involving the active time-lord carry amplified manifestation power during its reign.
The most widespread Hellenistic timing technique. Starting from the Ascendant at birth (Age 0), the profection advances by one zodiac sign per year of life in zodiacal order.

The planet that rules the profected sign activated for a given year of life. This planet becomes the primary time-lord, and its natal condition, house placement, and transits dictate the year's main story arc.

• Annual Profection: 30° per year (1 sign per year).
• Monthly Profection: 2.5° per month (1 sign every 2.5 months / 12 signs per year).
• Daily Profection: ~1° every 12 days.

A classical Persian and Arabic time-lord system that assigns fixed planetary periods to a lifespan totaling 75 years:
• Day Birth Sequence: Sun (10 yrs) → Venus (8 yrs) → Mercury (13 yrs) → Moon (9 yrs) → Saturn (11 yrs) → Jupiter (12 yrs) → Mars (7 yrs) → North Node (3 yrs) → South Node (2 yrs).
• Night Birth Sequence: Moon (9 yrs) → Saturn (11 yrs) → Jupiter (12 yrs) → Mars (7 yrs) → Sun (10 yrs) → Venus (8 yrs) → Mercury (13 yrs) → North Node (3 yrs) → South Node (2 yrs).
Subdivisions of each major Firdaria period (excluding the Nodes) divided into 7 equal sub-periods, ruled sequentially by the major period ruler followed by the Chaldean planetary order.

A potent Hellenistic time-lord technique preserved by Vettius Valens that "releases" time periods from the Lot of Spirit (governing career, action, and calling) or the Lot of Fortune (governing health, body, and material fortune).

• Level 1 (General Periods / L1): Major decades-long periods governed by the sign's planetary years.
• Level 2 (Sub-periods / L2): Months-long sub-periods (each L1 year = 1 L2 month).
• Level 3 (Weeks / L3): ~2.5-day sub-periods.
• Level 4 (Days / L4): ~5-hour micro-periods.

entries.term: Planetary Minor Years (Least Years of the Planets)
entries.text:
The baseline time-period durations assigned to signs during Zodiacal Releasing based on synodic recurrence cycles:
• Saturn (Capricorn/Aquarius): 30 years.
• Jupiter (Sagittarius/Pisces): 12 years.
• Mars (Aries/Scorpio): 15 years.
• Sun (Leo): 19 years (Metonic cycle).
• Venus (Taurus/Libra): 8 years.
• Mercury (Gemini/Virgo): 20 years.
• Moon (Cancer): 25 years.

A critical transition during Zodiacal Releasing when a sequence reaches the end of its 12-sign cycle and "jumps" to the opposite sign instead of repeating, marking a dramatic turning point or career transformation.

Periods during Zodiacal Releasing when Level 2 or Level 3 releases into a sign that sits in an angular house (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) relative to the Lot of Spirit or Fortune, triggering intense activity and high public visibility.

An ancient planetary timing model dividing human life into seven fixed developmental stages:
1. Moon (Infancy / Ages 0–4): Physical growth and instinctual dependency.
2. Mercury (Childhood / Ages 4–14): Language, learning, and cognition.
3. Venus (Youth / Ages 14–22): Puberty, romance, social attraction, and art.
4. Sun (Young Adulthood / Ages 22–41): Mastery, career drive, and ambition.
5. Mars (Mature Adulthood / Ages 41–56): Executive action, authority, and struggle.
6. Jupiter (Elder / Ages 56–68): Wisdom, counsel, expansion, and philosophy.
7. Saturn (Old Age / Ages 68+): Contraction, detachment, boundaries, and legacy.
An annual horoscope cast for the exact moment the transiting Sun returns to its exact natal zodiacal longitude. Serves as the primary overview map for the upcoming year.

• Non-Precessed (Tropical) Return: Cast for the exact tropical longitude of the natal Sun.
• Precessed (Sidereal) Return: Adjusts for the Precession of the Equinoxes (~50.26" of arc per year / 1° every 72 years), shifting the return time by several hours.

Calculating the Solar Return chart for the native's exact geographic location on their birthday (or current residence) rather than their birthplace, altering the return chart's angles and house cusps.
A monthly horoscope cast every 27.32 days (tropical month) when the Moon returns to its exact natal position, mapping emotional themes for the upcoming month.
Erecting a return chart for a time prior to birth calculated converse to the age of the native.

• Mercury Return: Occurs roughly once a year; highlights mental projects, contracts, and communication.
• Venus Return: Occurs every 247 days (or 8-year synodic cycle); highlights relationships, aesthetics, finances, and personal values.
• Mars Return: Occurs every ~2 years (687 days); highlights energy, physical projects, ambition, and boundary assertion.
• Jupiter Return: Occurs every 11.86 years (~12 years); highlights major growth, higher education, travel, and luck.
• Saturn Return: Occurs every 29.5 years (~ages 29–30 and 58–60); marks an essential rite of passage, structural maturity, confronting limits, and stepping into adult authority.
A horoscope cast for the exact moment a transiting planet crosses 0°00'00" of a sign (especially Sun entering 0° Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn) to forecast global or mundane events.
The physical positions of planets in the sky at any given calendar date, evaluated against the natal chart to provide external timing triggers.

A fast-moving transiting body—most notably the Sun, Mars, or New/Full Moons—that forms an exact contact to a sensitive natal point while a heavy outer-planet transit is active, acting as the immediate catalyst that ignites the event.

The allowable angular distance for transits. Fast inner planets use tight orbs (1°–2°), while outer heavy planets (Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) exert a psychological orb of 3°–5° as they approach exactness.

Occurs when a transiting planet freezes in longitude (turning Retrograde or Direct) within 1° of a natal planet or angle. Concentrates transit energy to a maximum focal point, lingering for weeks or months.

The standard sequence formed when an outer planet transits over a natal point three times due to retrograde motion:
1. First Direct Pass: Initial awareness, surprise, or introduction of the theme.
2. Retrograde Pass: Internal processing, review, resistance, or revision.
3. Final Direct Pass: Resolution, integration, physical manifestation, and closure.
Formulating aspects between transiting planets and secondary progressed planets/angles, bridging outer circumstances directly to inner psychological readiness.

A progressive timing system introduced by Troinski where 1 day of planetary motion after birth equals 1 lunar month (27.32 days) of life. Used to track rapid emotional developments and month-by-month timing.
A system where 1 lunar month (27.32 days) after birth equals 1 year of life.
Calculating any progressive or directional method backward into prenatal time (prior to birth) to evaluate inherited patterns or pre-natal conditioning.
Sub-divisional directional methods that progress the 12th-parts (Duodecatemoria / 2.5° arcs) or 9th-parts (Novenaria / 3°20' arcs) of signs to time micro-events.
A return chart cast every month when the transiting Moon reaches the exact natal phase angle (exact angular distance) relative to the transiting Sun that it held at birth.
Return charts calculated for the moment a transiting planet conjoins a progressed planet (e.g., Kinetic Lunar Return = transiting Moon conjoin secondary progressed Moon).
Graphic timelines or matrices plotting overlapping transit orbs, progressed aspects, and time-lord shifts to pinpoint peak event windows.

entries.text: The repressed, disowned, or unacknowledged parts of the psyche that the conscious ego rejects. In a horoscope, the shadow manifests through planets in the 12th House, afflicted Pluto or Saturn, Black Moon Lilith, or unintegrated hard aspect patterns.

• Anima: The unconscious feminine archetype within a male psyche, mapped by the placements and aspects of Venus and the Moon.
• Animus: The unconscious masculine archetype within a female psyche, mapped by the placements and aspects of Mars and the Sun.

entries.section: Depth Psychology & Jungian Archetypes in Astrology
entries.text: The Jungian archetype of psychological wholeness, central purpose, and spiritual integration, represented by the Sun at the center of the total chart mandala.

entries.section: Depth Psychology & Jungian Archetypes in Astrology
entries.text: The lifelong psychological journey of integrating disowned shadow elements, resolving planetary complexes, and harmonizing internal polarities to achieve self-realization.

entries.section: Depth Psychology & Jungian Archetypes in Astrology
entries.text: Formulated by C.G. Jung and physicist Wolfgang Pauli. The core theoretical foundation of astrology, asserting that events occurring simultaneously in space and time share a meaningful symbolic connection without physical cause and effect ("As above, so below").

entries.section: Depth Psychology & Jungian Archetypes in Astrology
entries.text: A subconscious defense mechanism where an individual disowns a planetary drive within themselves and "projects" it onto others (e.g., projecting an unacknowledged Pluto onto external "controlling enemies," or projecting Venus onto an idealized partner).

entries.section: Depth Psychology & Jungian Archetypes in Astrology
entries.text: An emotionally charged network of subconscious memories, wounds, and behavioral reactions structured around a specific planet (e.g., a "Saturn Complex" involving deep-seated fear of failure/authority, or a "Moon Complex" involving abandonment fears).

entries.term: Black Moon Lilith (The Primal Feminine / Refusal to Submit)
entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: The calculated lunar apogee (the point where the Moon is farthest from Earth in its orbit). Represents raw instinct, refusal to submit to societal suppression, sacred rage, exile, repressed desire, and uncorrupted authenticity.

entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: A secondary shadow point associated with intense psychological projections, emotional obsession, and purifying deep subconscious patterns.

entries.term: The Twelfth House (The Closet of Secrets / Subconscious Matrix)
entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: The house of solitude, hidden motives, ancestral conditioning, self-sabotage, mental health, and spiritual surrender. Planets placed here operate behind a veil, requiring conscious effort to bring into awareness.

entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: The primary driver of evolutionary death and rebirth. Governs deep psychological wounds, power dynamics, obsession, compulsion, survival instincts, and unearthing hidden truths.

entries.term: Chiron (The Wounded Healer / Core Soul Trauma)
entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: A Centaur body representing the systemic, unhealable wound carried by the soul. Governs compassion developed through personal pain, spiritual mentorship, and turning vulnerability into medicine for others.

entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: A Centaur associated with breaking intergenerational abuse, obsessive cycles, power abuses, and severing toxic karmic ties.

entries.section: Shadow Points, Dark Luminaries & Karmic Catalysts
entries.text: A Centaur representing sudden, irreversible tipping points, unlocking hidden family secrets, and unleashing long-suppressed psychological forces.

entries.section: Esoteric & Soul-Centered Astrology (Alice Bailey / Djwhal Khul Tradition)
entries.text: A branch of astrology focusing on the evolution of human consciousness, spiritual initiation, and the soul's divine purpose (The Consciousness Axis) rather than personal fortune or ego personality (The Form Axis).

entries.section: Esoteric & Soul-Centered Astrology (Alice Bailey / Djwhal Khul Tradition)
entries.text:
• Personality Level (Exoteric): Interpreting planets as ego drives, physical needs, and worldly reactions.
• Soul Level (Esoteric): Interpreting planets as channels for spiritual service, group consciousness, and divine intent.

entries.section: Esoteric & Soul-Centered Astrology (Alice Bailey / Djwhal Khul Tradition)
entries.text:
Alternative planetary rulers assigned to the twelve zodiac signs that become active as an individual awakens to soul-consciousness:
• Aries: Mercury (Soul) / Uranus (Hierarchical)
• Taurus: Vulcan (Soul) / Serpent (Hierarchical)
• Gemini: Venus (Soul) / Earth (Hierarchical)
• Cancer: Neptune (Soul) / Bacchus (Hierarchical)
• Leo: Sun (Soul) / Sun (Hierarchical)
• Virgo: Moon (Soul) / Jupiter (Hierarchical)
• Libra: Uranus (Soul) / Saturn (Hierarchical)
• Scorpio: Mars (Soul) / Mercury (Hierarchical)
• Sagittarius: Earth (Soul) / Mars (Hierarchical)
• Capricorn: Saturn (Soul) / Venus (Hierarchical)
• Aquarius: Jupiter (Soul) / Moon (Hierarchical)
• Pisces: Pluto (Soul) / Pluto (Hierarchical)

entries.term: The Seven Rays of Divine Energy
entries.section: Esoteric & Soul-Centered Astrology (Alice Bailey / Djwhal Khul Tradition)
entries.text:
Fundamental cosmic streams of energy governing all life, transmitted through specific planets and signs:
1. Ray 1 (Will or Power): Ruled by Pluto and Vulcan (transmitting through Aries, Leo, Capricorn).
2. Ray 2 (Love-Wisdom): Ruled by Sun and Jupiter (transmitting through Gemini, Virgo, Pisces).
3. Ray 3 (Active Intelligence): Ruled by Saturn and Earth (transmitting through Cancer, Libra, Capricorn).
4. Ray 4 (Harmony through Conflict): Ruled by Mercury (transmitting through Taurus, Scorpio, Sagittarius).
5. Ray 5 (Concrete Science / Knowledge): Ruled by Venus (transmitting through Leo, Sagittarius, Aquarius).
6. Ray 6 (Devotion and Idealism): Ruled by Mars and Neptune (transmitting through Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces).
7. Ray 7 (Ceremonial Order / Magic): Ruled by Uranus (transmitting through Aries, Cancer, Capricorn).

entries.term: The Form Axis vs. Consciousness Axis
entries.section: Esoteric & Soul-Centered Astrology (Alice Bailey / Djwhal Khul Tradition)
entries.text: The structural shift in chart interpretation where the Ascendant-Descendant axis represents the soul's emergence into physical form, and the Midheaven-IC axis represents the spiritual realization of divine authority.

entries.section: Karmic & Evolutionary Astrology (Jeffrey Wolf Green, Schulman, Jones)
entries.text: A framework founded by Jeffrey Wolf Green centered on Pluto and the Lunar Nodal axis to trace the soul’s evolutionary desires, past choices, and current life lessons.

entries.section: Karmic & Evolutionary Astrology (Jeffrey Wolf Green, Schulman, Jones)
entries.text: The foundational EA rule asserting that Pluto's sign and house position reveal the soul’s prior evolutionary desires and karmic attachments, while the Pluto Polarity Point (PPP)—the exact point 180° opposite Pluto—indicates the required evolutionary direction for the current life.

entries.section: Karmic & Evolutionary Astrology (Jeffrey Wolf Green, Schulman, Jones)
entries.text:
• South Node (Ketu): Represents past-life instincts, familiar habits, developed talents, and unwholesome comfort zones carried into this life.
• South Node Ruler: Reveals how the past-life orientation was applied and resolved.
• North Node (Rahu): Represents unfamiliar evolutionary growth, current life trajectory, and new psychological lessons to master.
• North Node Ruler: Indicates the practical tools required to fulfill the North Node's evolutionary mandate.

entries.term: Skipped Steps (Planets Squaring the Nodal Axis)
entries.section: Karmic & Evolutionary Astrology (Jeffrey Wolf Green, Schulman, Jones)
entries.text: Any planet forming an exact 90° square to the North and South Nodes. Indicates a developmental roadblock or unresolved evolutionary lesson from a past life that was interrupted and must be re-addressed in this lifetime.

entries.section: Karmic & Evolutionary Astrology (Jeffrey Wolf Green, Schulman, Jones)
entries.text: Martin Schulman’s interpretation of retrograde planets as internal "time warps" where past-life memories and subconscious habits blend into current experiences, requiring the native to re-live and refine those planetary drives.

entries.section: Karmic & Evolutionary Astrology (Jeffrey Wolf Green, Schulman, Jones)
entries.text: The opposition line formed by the South Node and North Node, representing the primary bridge between past conditioning and future growth.

A framework developed by philosopher Richard Tarnas (Cosmos and Psyche) viewing planets as dynamic, multidimensional archetypal principles (based on Jung, Plato, and James Hillman) that manifest co-creatively through human consciousness.

Pioneered by Dane Rudhyar, viewing the chart as a holistic mandala for self-actualization. Focuses on the transpersonal outer planets (Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) as cosmic agents designed to break through ego limitations.

Applying Roberto Assagioli’s model of Psychosynthesis to the birth chart, treating each planet as an internal subpersonality (e.g., Mars as the Inner Warrior, Venus as the Lover, Saturn as the Judge) that must be integrated into a unified psyche.
The central identity balance formed by the Sun (conscious ego/will), Moon (subconscious emotion/habit), and Ascendant (outer persona/adaptability).

An unconscious defense mechanism triggered by harsh aspect configurations (like squares or oppositions) where an individual splits off one planet's energy (e.g., rejecting Mars anger) and projects it onto external circumstances or partners.
Intense periods during major outer planet transits (e.g., Uranus Opposition, Neptune Square, Pluto Conjunction) where existing ego structures dissolve to allow spiritual awakening.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text: The primary visual matrix and energy map used in Human Design to depict an individual's mechanics, centers, channels, and gates.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text:
Derived from the Hindu-Brahmin chakra system, these centers process life force energy. They are either Defined (colored in, consistent, reliable energy) or Undefined/Completely Open (white, receptive, prone to conditioning, and potential sources of wisdom):
1. Head Center: Inspiration and mental pressure.
2. Ajna Center: Conceptualization and mental processing.
3. Throat Center: Expression, manifestation, and action.
4. G Center (Identity): Identity, love, direction, and the seat of the Magnetic Monopole.
5. Heart (Ego) Center: Willpower, material drive, and self-worth.
6. Solar Plexus Center: Emotional wave, desire, and awareness.
7. Sacral Center: Generative life force, response, work capacity, and sexuality.
8. Spleen Center: Intuitive survival, health, instinct, and time awareness.
9. Root Center: Adrenaline, stress pressure, and physical momentum.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text:
The primary classification of aura mechanics dictating how an individual correctly navigates life:
• Manifestors (~9%): Closed, repelling aura; strategy is to inform before initiating action to minimize social resistance.
• Generators (~37%): Open, enveloping aura; strategy is to wait to respond via Sacral sound/impulse.
• Manifesting Generators (~33%): Fast, multi-passionate variant of the Generator; strategy is to wait to respond, then inform before acting.
• Projectors (~20%): Absorbing, focused aura; strategy is to wait for formal recognition and invitation to share guidance.
• Reflectors (~1%): Completely open, sampling aura; strategy is to wait a full 28.5-day Lunar Cycle before making major life decisions.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text: The specific intelligence center that overrides the mind to guide correct choices (e.g., Emotional Solar Plexus, Sacral, Splenic, Ego-Manifested, Self-Projected, Environmental, Lunar).

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text:
• Gates: The 64 specific hexagram activations derived from the I Ching, mapped around the Rave Mandala.
• Channels: Connective energy lines linking two centers. When both gates on a channel are defined, the entire channel colors in, creating consistent life-force definition.
• Tantric Channels: Channels 5–15 (Rhythm), 14–2 (Beat), and 29–46 (Discovery) linking the Sacral to the G Center.
• Integration Channel: A self-empowerment network comprising Gates 34, 57, 10, and 20.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text:
A fractional code (e.g., 1/3, 3/5, 5/1, 6/2) derived from the hexagram line numbers (Lines 1 through 6) of the Sun/Earth placements, defining one's costume or archetype in society:
• Line 1: Investigator | Line 2: Hermit | Line 3: Martyr | Line 4: Opportunist | Line 5: Heretic | Line 6: Role Model.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text:
• Personality (Black / Right Column): Conscious placements calculated for the exact birth time.
• Design (Red / Left Column): Unconscious physical/ancestral body placements calculated ~88 days (88° solar arc) prior to birth.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text: The four arrows on the BodyGraph representing Digestion/Dietary Regimen, Environment, Perspective, and Motivation.

entries.section: The Human Design System (The Science of Differentiation)
entries.text: The combination of the Personality and Design Sun and Earth gates (accounting for 70% of the chart's energy), defining life purpose.

entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: The complete matrix formed by four vertical columns—Year, Month, Day, and Hour Pillars. Each pillar contains one Heavenly Stem (upper row) and one Earthly Branch (lower row).

entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: Celestial attributes representing the Five Elements split into Yin and Yang polarities: Jia (Yang Wood), Yi (Yin Wood), Bing (Yang Fire), Ding (Yin Fire), Wu (Yang Earth), Ji (Yin Earth), Geng (Yang Metal), Xin (Yin Metal), Ren (Yang Water), and Gui (Yin Water).

entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: Terrestrial realizations representing the 12 zodiacal animals: Zi (Rat), Chou (Ox), Yin (Tiger), Mao (Rabbit), Chen (Dragon), Si (Snake), Wu (Horse), Wei (Goat), Shen (Monkey), You (Rooster), Xu (Dog), and Hai (Pig).

entries.term: Day Master (Tian Gan of the Day Pillar)
entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: The central anchor of the Ba Zi chart (representing ~70% of a person's psychological archetype). Evaluated against the season and surrounding elements to determine whether it is Strong, Weak, Prosperous, or Dead.

entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: Heavenly stems embedded inside Earthly Branches, classified into Growth, Cardinal, and Graveyard branches.

entries.term: Five Factors & The Ten Gods (Shi Shen)
entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text:
Relational interactions between the Day Master and other stems based on the Cycles of Creation (Sheng) and Control (Ke):
• Parallel / Friends & Rob Wealth: Stems matching the Day Master's element.
• Output (Eating God & Hurting Officer): Element produced by the Day Master.
• Wealth (Direct Wealth & Indirect Wealth): Element controlled by the Day Master.
• Power / Officer (Direct Officer & Seven Killings): Element controlling the Day Master.
• Resource (Direct Resource & Indirect Resource): Element producing the Day Master.

entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: 10-year dynamic energy cycles calculated from the Month Pillar based on gender and stem polarity, revealing timing shifts across a lifespan.

entries.term: Twelve Stages of Chi (Shi Er Chang Sheng)
entries.section: Ba Zi / Four Pillars of Destiny (Chinese Metaphysics)
entries.text: The 12-stage life cycle of an element's strength: Growth (Chang Sheng), Childhood, Adulthood, Maturity (Di Wang), Decline, Sickness, Death, and Burial/Graveyard.

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text: The foundational number obtained by summing all digits in a complete birth date down to a single digit (or Master Number). Represents the primary pathway and evolutionary purpose of a lifespan.

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text:
Double-digit repeating numbers that carry heightened spiritual potential, high-frequency intuition, and practical mastery:
• 11: High intuition, spiritual idealism, and illumination.
• 22/4: The Master Builder; combining vision with practical execution.

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text:
• Basic / Physical Plane (1, 4, 7): Physical action, practicality, activity, and body endurance.
• Soul / Feeling Plane (2, 5, 8): High self, intuition, emotion, compassion, and artistic wisdom.
• Mind / Thinking Plane (3, 6, 9): Memory, intellect, creative analysis, responsibility, and idealism.

entries.term: The Birth Chart Grid & Arrows of Individuality
entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text: A 3x3 numeric grid where birth date digits are placed. Complete lines form "Arrows of Strength" (e.g., Arrow of Determination 1-5-9, Arrow of Practicality 1-4-7, Arrow of Intellect 3-6-9); missing lines form "Arrows of Weakness".

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text: The number of the specific day of the month on which birth occurred, representing secondary talents and outer personality expression.

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text: A recurring 9-year cycle tracking individual growth through distinct annual themes from Inception (Year 1) through Peak (Year 9).

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text: The universal global frequency calculated by summing the digits of a calendar year.

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text: Four calculated life peaks derived using the mystical number 36 minus the Ruling Number, identifying major maturity benchmarks.

entries.section: Pythagorean Numerology & The Science of Numbers
entries.text:
• Soul Urge (Heart's Desire): Calculated from the vowels of a full name.
• Outer Expression: Calculated from the consonants of a full name.

• The Emperor = Aries

• The Magician = Mercury | The High Priestess = Moon | The Empress = Venus | The Tower = Mars | Wheel of Fortune = Jupiter | The World = Saturn | The Sun = Sun | The Fool = Uranus | The Hanged Man = Neptune | Judgment = Pluto.
The 36 numbered cards (2s through 10s of Wands, Cups, Swords, Pentacles) mapped directly to the 36 Chaldean Faces around the Wheel of the Year.
Kings, Queens, Knights, and Pages assigned to elemental cross-quadrants and 30° sectors spanning adjacent signs.
The 22 paths connecting the 10 Sephiroth on the Tree of Life, corresponding directly to the 22 Major Arcana trumps and planetary/sign channels.

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: The foundational 12-sign zodiac map anchored to physical fixed star constellations using an Ayanamsha correction (e.g., Lahiri).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: 13°20' lunar divisions ruled by specific deities and planetary lords (Ketu, Venus, Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: A 120-year planetary time-lord cycle starting from the native's birth Nakshatra Moon placement, unfolding major periods (Mahadashas) and sub-periods (Antardashas / Bhuktis).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text:
Harmonic subdivisions of the chart wheel used for granular analysis:
• Navamsa (D9): 1/9th division; the primary soul chart, marriage indicator, and ultimate test of planetary strength.
• Hora (D2): Wealth; Drekkana (D3): Siblings/courage; Dasamsa (D10): Career.

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: Specific multi-planet alignments producing distinct worldly results (e.g., Raja Yoga for power/status, Dhana Yoga for wealth, Chandra-Mangala Yoga for enterprise).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: Natural (Naisargika) or temporal (Jaimini) significators (e.g., Lagnadhipati = Ascendant lord, Yogakaraka = functional benefic).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: The North (Rahu) and South (Ketu) Lunar Nodes governing intense worldly desire (Rahu) and spiritual liberation/detachment (Ketu).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: Terrestrial places measured relative to the Lagna (Ascendant) or Chandra Lagna (Moon Ascendant).

entries.section: Jyotish / Vedic Astrology (The Science of Light)
entries.text: Calculated sensitive points used to evaluate male (Beeja) and female (Kshetra) reproductive vitality and fertility.

Formulated by Jim Lewis. Projects a birth chart's planetary positions onto a global terrestrial map, drawing lines where planets were rising (ASC), culminating (MC), setting (DSC), or anti-culminating (IC) at birth.

• MC Lines: Career, public visibility, vocation, and reputational peak.
• ASC Lines: Personal identity, physical embodiment, self-activation, and health.
• IC Lines: Private life, real estate, emotional roots, and family foundation.
• DSC Lines: Partnerships, key relationships, open interactions, and social contracts.
Relocates chart vectors onto a local horizon compass (Azimuth and Altitude), drawing directional lines across cities, rooms, or homes.
Mapping the 360° terrestrial globe directly to the 360° ecliptic (0° Greenwich = 0° Aries or 0° Libra) to evaluate mundane geographic locations.

Groundbreaking statistical research by Michel and Françoise Gauquelin demonstrating significant correlations between planetary positions in "critical sectors" (just after rising or culminating / Houses 12 and 9) and professional success:
• Mars Effect: Prominent in champions and athletes.
• Jupiter Effect: Prominent in actors, politicians, and executives.
• Saturn Effect: Prominent in scientists and doctors.
• Moon Effect: Prominent in writers and artists.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A chart cast for the exact minute, hour, date, and geographic location where an astrologer receives and clearly understands a specific pressing question from a client (Querent).

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: The person asking the question in a horary chart, represented by the 1st House cusp, its ruling planet, and the Moon.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: The person, object, animal, or matter being asked about, represented by the specific house governing that topic and its ruling planet.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A set of classical checks evaluating whether a horary chart is safe, valid, and reliable to judge.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text:
Specific traditional warning rules signaling that a horary chart may be premature, stale, or unjudgeable:
• ASC Less Than 3°: The question is premature; circumstances are still forming and events are not yet ripe.
• ASC Greater Than 27°: The question is too late; the matter has already been decided or is past repair.
• Moon in Via Combusta (15° Libra to 15° Scorpio): The Moon is in the "Burned Way," indicating extreme emotional distress, fear, or instability (except when conjoined the fortunate star Spica at 24° Libra).
• Saturn in the 1st House: The querent's judgment is impaired, or the question is flawed.
• Saturn in the 7th House: The astrologer's judgment may be compromised (unless the astrologer is the 7th house subject).

entries.term: Turning the Chart (Derived Houses in Horary)
entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Re-orienting house numbering to treat the Quesited's house as a temporary 1st house (e.g., evaluating the partner's money by looking at the 2nd house from the 7th house, which is the 8th house of the chart).

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Occurs when two significators are moving toward an exact applying aspect with each other, promising a positive resolution ("Yes") to the question.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Occurs when two significators are applying to an exact aspect, but a third, faster planet forms an aspect to one of them first, "prohibiting" or blocking the agreement.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Occurs when Planet A applies to Planet B, but before the aspect becomes exact, Planet B changes signs or forms an aspect with Planet C, "frustrating" the outcome.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: When a third, heavier planet intervenes by aspect to sever the connection between two significators.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Occurs when a significator applies toward another planet, but turns retrograde before the aspect reaches exactness, indicating a change of mind or backing out of an agreement.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: The Moon making no further major applying aspects before leaving its current sign; in horary, it signifies "nothing will come of the matter" or "the situation will not change."

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: When two non-aspecting significators both apply to a heavier, slower third planet, which collects their light and brings the matter to fruition through a third party.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: When a fast planet separates from one significator and immediately applies to another significator, carrying the energy between them via a mediator or messenger.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: The practice of choosing an auspicious future moment to initiate an action (e.g., launching a business, marriage, surgery) by fortunating the Ascendant, its ruler, the Moon, and placing malefic planets in cadent houses.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: The technique of superimposing one person's natal planetary degrees directly onto another person's natal chart wheel to evaluate inter-chart aspects and house activations.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A mathematical chart calculated by finding the exact midpoints between two individuals' natal planets and angles (e.g., Composite Sun = Midpoint of Person A's Sun and Person B's Sun). Represents the independent relationship entity itself as a third system.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A relationship chart calculated for the exact mathematical midpoint in time (date/time) and geographic space (latitude/longitude) between two births; yields a fully functional astronomical chart that can be progressed and transited.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A powerful relational reinforcement where Person A's Planet X aspects Person B's Planet Y, AND Person B's Planet X aspects Person A's Planet Y (e.g., Person A's Venus trine Person B's Mars AND Person B's Venus square Person A's Mars).

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: When one person's personal planets (Sun, Moon, Venus, Mars) or angles form tight conjunctions to another person's North or South Lunar Node, indicating a powerful feeling of destiny, karmic binding, or soul-contract lessons.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A synastry alignment where one person's Saturn forms a conjunction, trine, or square to another person's Venus; provides long-term commitment, loyalty, and practical endurance, though harsh aspects require overcoming coolness or restriction.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: When one person's personal planet or angle conjoins another person's Vertex or Antivertex, triggering sudden, transformative relationship catalysts or feeling like a "fated encounter."

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Evaluating which house in Person A's chart is occupied by Person B's planets (e.g., Person B's Sun falling in Person A's 8th house creates deep emotional, psychological, or financial intensity).

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A global chart calculated for the exact moment the transiting Sun crosses 0°00'00" Aries (the Vernal Equinox) for a nation's capital, predicting political, economic, and social conditions for the year.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: The conjunctions of Jupiter and Saturn occurring every 20 years. Every ~200 years, these conjunctions shift into a new element (Fire → Earth → Air → Water), signaling monumental historical, economic, and civilizational shifts (e.g., the 2020 shift from Earth to Air signs).

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: Formulated by André Barbault; a mathematical index that sums the angular distances between all outer planets (Jupiter through Pluto). Peaks correlate with global stability and progress, while deep troughs correlate with world wars, crises, and epidemics.

entries.chapter: Branches: Horary, Synastry, Mundane, Medical & More
entries.text: A recurring 18-year, 11-day eclipse cycle (spanning 1,200 to 1,500 years per series) governed by specific geometric dynamics from the North or South Pole, shaping generational geopolitical shifts.

• 1st Harmonic (Radix): The standard natal birth chart; the baseline physical reality.

entries.text:
Planetary roles assigned dynamically in every birth chart based on which planets hold the highest to lowest degree longitudes (excluding Rahu/Ketu):

2. Amatyakaraka (AmK): The 2nd highest degree planet; represents career, vocation, professional intellect, and life's primary work.
3. Bhratrukaraka (BK): The 3rd highest degree planet; represents siblings, companions, teachers, and spiritual gurus.
4. Matrukaraka (MK): The 4th highest degree planet; represents mother, home, emotional security, and real estate.
5. Putrakaraka (PK): The 5th highest degree planet; represents children, creative intelligence, disciples, and education.
6. Gnatikaraka (GK): The 6th highest degree planet; represents rivals, obstacles, conflicts, physical illness, and systemic tests.
7. Darakaraka (DK): The planet with the lowest degree longitude; represents the spouse, marriage partner, intimacy, and business associates.

A comprehensive table listing the exact spatial coordinates of every planet in a birth chart across four distinct coordinate systems:
• Celestial Longitude (λ): Distance along the ecliptic (0°–360°).
• Celestial Latitude (β): Angular distance north or south of the ecliptic.
• Right Ascension (α / RA): Distance measured along the celestial equator in hours/minutes or degrees (0°–360°).
• Declination (δ): Angular distance north (+) or south (-) of the celestial equator.
The shortest distance along the celestial equator (in RA) between a planet and the local meridian (Midheaven or IC).

The exact time (expressed in equatorial degrees) required for a celestial body to travel from the horizon to its culmination point on the meridian (Diurnal Semi-Arc if above horizon; Nocturnal Semi-Arc if below).
The relative latitude elevation used in Placidian primary directions to calculate intermediate house circles and direct planets proportionally along their semi-arcs.
